Supports dashboards (requires dashboardUid or provisioningPreview), panels (requires dashboardUid or provisioningPreview, plus panelId), and Explore queries (requires datasourceUid and optionally queries). For dashboard and panel links, provisioningPreview points at a dashboard staged on a provisioning repository branch (e.g. a git-sync PR preview). For explore links, the time range and queries are embedded inside the Grafana explore state. Set shorten=true to also attempt a /goto/<uid> short URL; if shortening fails, the full deeplink is returned.

dashboardUid.description: Dashboard UID (for stored dashboards). Mutually exclusive with provisioningPreview for dashboard and panel types.

datasourceUid.description: Datasource UID (required for explore type)

repo.description: Provisioning repository slug. List repositories via list_provisioning_repositories if unknown.

path.description: Path to the dashboard file within the repository, relative to its root.

ref.description: Branch or commit SHA. Defaults to the repository's main branch when omitted.

pullRequestUrl.description: Upstream pull request URL to surface in Grafana's preview banner.

provisioningPreview.description: Identifies a dashboard staged on a provisioning repository branch (e.g. a git-sync PR preview). Mutually exclusive with dashboardUid for dashboard and panel types.

queries.description: List of query objects for explore links (e.g. [{"refId":"A","expr":"up"}])

queryParams.description: Additional URL query parameters (for dashboard/panel types)

resourceType.description: Type of resource: dashboard, panel, or explore

shorten.description: If true, try to shorten the generated URL to /goto/<uid>. If shortening fails, return the original deeplink.

tools.name: get_alert_group
tools.description: Get a specific alert group from Grafana OnCall by its ID. Returns the full alert group details, including the most recent alert and its raw payload when the OnCall API provides them. Alert payloads carry integration-specific fingerprints (for example Sentry's payload.data.event.hashes or Alertmanager's payload.alerts[].fingerprint) that identify recurring alerts across different alert groups.

alertGroupId.description: The ID of the alert group to retrieve

tools.name: get_annotation_tags
tools.description: Returns annotation tags with optional filtering by tag name. Only the provided filters are applied.

limit.description: Max results, default 100

tools.name: get_annotations
tools.description: Fetch Grafana annotations using filters such as dashboard UID, time range and tags.

dashboardUid.description: Filter by dashboard UID

limit.description: Max results default 100

matchAny.description: If true, match any tag (OR). If false, match all tags (AND). Default: false

tags.description: Filter by tags. Multiple tags allowed; use matchAny to control AND/OR logic

type.description: annotation or alert

tools.name: get_assertions
tools.description: Get assertion summary for a given entity with its type, name, env, site, namespace, and a time range

endTime.description: The end time in RFC3339 format (e.g. 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z) or relative format (e.g. now)

entityName.description: The name of the entity to list

entityType.description: The type of the entity to list (e.g. Service, Node, Pod, etc.)

env.description: The env of the entity to list

namespace.description: The namespace of the entity to list

site.description: The site of the entity to list

startTime.description: The start time in RFC3339 format (e.g. 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z) or relative format (e.g. now-1h)

tools.name: get_current_oncall_users
tools.description: Get the list of users currently on-call for a specific Grafana OnCall schedule ID. Returns the schedule ID, name, and a list of detailed user objects for those currently on call.

scheduleId.description: The ID of the schedule to get current on-call users for

tools.name: get_dashboard_by_uid
tools.description: Retrieves the complete dashboard, including panels, variables, and settings, for a specific dashboard identified by its UID. Pass optional version to load a saved snapshot instead of the current dashboard. Saved snapshots are fetched through Grafana's legacy versions API, so 'apiVersion' is omitted and 'meta' is partial: only version, createdBy, and created are populated. For current (non-versioned) fetches, the response includes 'apiVersion' and 'isV2': when 'isV2' is true the dashboard uses the v2 schema (panels live under 'elements' keyed by name, arranged by 'layout'; variables under 'variables'), otherwise it is classic v1 ('panels[]' with 'templating.list'). WARNING: Large dashboards can consume significant context window space. Consider using get_dashboard_summary for overview or get_dashboard_property for specific data instead.

version.description: Optional saved version. Omit for the current dashboard

tools.name: get_dashboard_panel_queries
tools.description: Retrieve panel queries from a Grafana dashboard. Supports all datasource types (Prometheus, Loki, CloudWatch, SQL, etc.) and row-nested panels. Optionally filter to a specific panel by ID with `panelId`. Optionally provide `variables` for template variable substitution, which populates `processedQuery` and `requiredVariables` fields. Returns an array of objects with fields: title, query (raw expression), datasource (object with uid and type), and optionally processedQuery, refId, requiredVariables, and target. Targets built in a visual editor (CloudWatch metric search, InfluxDB query builder) have no string expression: those return an empty query plus `target`, the panel's raw query JSON. Run those with run_panel_query rather than a query tool.

panelId.description: Optional panel ID to filter to a specific panel

tools.name: get_dashboard_property
tools.description: Get specific parts of a dashboard using JSONPath expressions to minimize context window usage. JSONPath targets the dashboard's native schema. Classic v1 paths: '$.title' (title)\, '$.panels[*].title' (all panel titles)\, '$.panels[0]' (first panel)\, '$.templating.list' (variables)\, '$.annotations.list' (saved dashboard annotation queries/definitions)\, '$.tags' (tags)\, '$.panels[*].targets[*].expr' (all queries). v2 dashboards (see isV2 from get_dashboard_by_uid) use different paths: '$.title'\, '$.elements' (panels\, keyed by name)\, '$.variables' (variables)\, '$.annotations'. Use this instead of get_dashboard_by_uid when you only need specific dashboard properties.

jsonPath.description: JSONPath expression to extract specific data (e.g., '$.panels[0].title' for first panel title, '$.panels[*].title' for all panel titles, '$.templating.list' for variables, '$.annotations.list' for saved dashboard annotation queries/definitions)

tools.name: get_dashboard_summary
tools.description: Get a compact summary of a dashboard including title\, panel count\, panel types\, variables\, and other metadata without the full JSON. Use this for dashboard overview and planning modifications without consuming large context windows.

tools.name: get_datasource
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific datasource by UID or name. Returns the full datasource model, including name, type, URL, access settings, JSON data, and secure JSON field status. Provide either uid or name; uid takes priority if both are given.

name.description: The name of the datasource. Used if UID is not provided.

uid.description: The UID of the datasource. If provided, takes priority over name.

tools.name: get_doc
tools.description: Fetch a Grafana documentation page. Set outline_only=true to get the heading structure first, then call again with a section name for bounded retrieval.

limit.description: Max lines to return (default ~80)

outline_only.description: Return only the heading outline (use to discover section names before fetching content)

section.description: Heading text to extract (returns only that section)

tools.name: get_incident
tools.description: Get a single incident by ID. Returns the full incident details including title, status, severity, labels, custom fields, timestamps, and other metadata.

id.description: The ID of the incident to retrieve

tools.name: get_oncall_shift
tools.description: Get detailed information for a specific Grafana OnCall shift using its ID. A shift represents a designated time period within a schedule when users are actively on-call. Returns the full shift details.

shiftId.description: The ID of the shift to get details for

tools.name: get_panel_image
tools.description: Render a Grafana dashboard panel or full dashboard as a PNG image. Returns the image as base64 encoded data. Requires the Grafana Image Renderer service to be installed. Either dashboardUid (for stored dashboards) or provisioningPreview (for dashboards staged on a provisioning repository branch, e.g. a git-sync PR) must be supplied. Use this for generating visual snapshots of dashboards for reports, alerts, or presentations.

dashboardUid.description: The UID of a stored dashboard containing the panel. Required unless provisioningPreview is provided.

height.description: Height of the rendered image in pixels. Defaults to 500

panelId.description: The ID of the panel to render. If omitted, the entire dashboard is rendered

repo.description: Provisioning repository slug. List repositories via /apis/provisioning.grafana.app/v0alpha1/namespaces/default/repositories if unknown.

path.description: Path to the dashboard file within the repository, relative to its root.

ref.description: Branch or commit SHA to render from. Defaults to the repository's main branch when omitted.

provisioningPreview.description: Render a dashboard from a provisioning repository branch (e.g. a git-sync PR preview). Mutually exclusive with dashboardUid.

scale.description: Scale factor for the image (1-3). Defaults to 1

theme.description: Theme for the rendered image: light or dark. Defaults to dark

timeRange.description: Time range for the rendered image

timeout.description: Rendering timeout in seconds. Defaults to 60

variables.description: Dashboard variables to apply. Values can be a single string or an array of strings for multi-value variables (e.g., {"var-datasource": "prometheus", "var-instance": ["server1", "server2"]})

width.description: Width of the rendered image in pixels. Defaults to 1000

tools.name: get_plugin
tools.description: Check whether a Grafana plugin is installed and retrieve its details (name, version, type, enabled status). Returns installed=false when the plugin is not found. Use install_plugin when a plugin is not installed to install plugin after confirming this action with the user.

tools.name: get_sift_analysis
tools.description: Retrieves a specific analysis from an investigation by its UUID. The investigation ID and analysis ID should be provided as strings in UUID format.

analysisId.description: The UUID of the specific analysis to retrieve

investigationId.description: The UUID of the investigation as a string (e.g. '02adab7c-bf5b-45f2-9459-d71a2c29e11b')

tools.name: get_sift_investigation
tools.description: Retrieves an existing Sift investigation by its UUID. The ID should be provided as a string in UUID format (e.g. '02adab7c-bf5b-45f2-9459-d71a2c29e11b').

id.description: The UUID of the investigation as a string (e.g. '02adab7c-bf5b-45f2-9459-d71a2c29e11b')

tools.name: get_snapshot
tools.description: Get a Grafana snapshot by key, including snapshot metadata and dashboard payload.

tools.name: get_tempo_trace
tools.description: Retrieve a specific trace by ID

datasourceUid.description: UID of the tempo datasource to query

tools.name: get_tempo_traceql_docs
tools.description: Retrieve TraceQL reference documentation with examples, covering attribute filters, aggregates, structural operators, and metrics queries. Consult this before writing a non-trivial TraceQL query, or after one returns an error or no results.

topic.description: Which section of the TraceQL reference to retrieve: 'basic' for attribute and duration filters, 'aggregates' for count/avg/sum and by() grouping, 'structural' for parent/child and descendant operators, 'metrics' for rate/quantile_over_time metrics queries

tools.name: grafana_api_request
tools.description: Make an authenticated HTTP request to the Grafana API. Similar to 'gh api' for GitHub. Supports any Grafana API endpoint with optional jq-style response filtering. Use this for API endpoints that don't have a dedicated tool.

body.description: Request body (JSON string). Used with POST, PUT, and PATCH requests.

endpoint.description: The API path relative to the Grafana base URL (e.g. '/api/org', '/api/dashboards/uid/abc123'). Must start with '/'.

headers.description: Additional HTTP headers to include in the request.

jq.description: A jq expression to filter or transform the JSON response (e.g. '.dashboards[] | .title').

method.description: HTTP method. Defaults to GET

tools.name: install_plugin
tools.description: Install a Grafana plugin by its plugin ID. If the version is not already confirmed with the user, omit it вЂ” the tool will look up the latest version and return it for confirmation before installing.

version.description: The exact version to install. Must be confirmed with the user before calling вЂ” if unknown, omit this field to look up the latest version first.

tools.name: list_alert_groups
tools.description: List alert groups from Grafana OnCall with filtering options. Supports filtering by alert group ID, route ID, integration ID, state (new, acknowledged, resolved, silenced), team ID, time range, labels, and name. For time ranges, use format '{start}_{end}' ISO 8601 timestamp range (e.g., '2025-01-19T00:00:00_2025-01-19T23:59:59' for a specific day). For labels, use format 'key:value' (e.g., ['env:prod', 'severity:high']). Returns a list of alert group objects with their details. Supports pagination.

id.description: Filter by specific alert group ID

labels.description: Filter by labels in format key:value (e.g., ['env:prod', 'severity:high'])

startedAt.description: Filter by time range in format '{start}_{end}' ISO 8601 timestamp range (UTC assumed, no timezone indicator needed) (e.g., '2025-01-19T00:00:00_2025-01-19T23:59:59')

state.description: Filter by alert group state (one of: new, acknowledged, resolved, silenced)

tools.name: list_dashboard_versions
tools.description: List saved versions of a Grafana dashboard. Returns compact metadata: version number, author, timestamp, and save message. Use get_dashboard_by_uid with version to fetch a snapshot.

limit.description: Maximum number of versions to return

start.description: Version to start from. Only versions at or below this number are returned

tools.name: list_datasources
tools.description: List all configured datasources in Grafana. Use this to discover available datasources and their UIDs. Supports filtering by type and/or name (case-insensitive substring match) and pagination.

limit.description: Maximum number of datasources to return (max 100)

name.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the datasource name. For example, 'prod' matches datasources named 'prometheus-prod-eu' and 'loki-prod-us'. Useful on instances with many datasources where filtering by type alone returns too many results.

offset.description: Number of datasources to skip for pagination

type.description: The type of datasources to search for. For example, 'prometheus', 'loki', 'tempo', etc...

tools.name: list_incident_custom_fields
tools.description: List the custom fields configured for Grafana incidents, including their type and, for select fields, the options that may be chosen. Use this to discover which fields exist and which values are valid before setting them with create_incident or update_incident.

includeArchived.description: Whether to include archived custom fields. Archived fields cannot be set on new incidents but may still hold values on older ones

tools.name: list_incidents
tools.description: List Grafana incidents. Allows filtering by status ('active', 'resolved') and optionally including drill incidents. Returns a preview list with basic details, and custom field values if requested.

includeCustomFields.description: Whether to include each incident's custom field values. Off by default because it costs an extra request and makes the response considerably larger

limit.description: The maximum number of incidents to return

status.description: The status of the incidents to include. Valid values: 'active', 'resolved'

tools.name: list_loki_label_names
tools.description: Lists all available label/field names (keys) found in logs within a specified Loki or VictoriaLogs datasource and time range. Returns a list of unique label strings (e.g., `["app", "env", "pod"]`). If the time range is not provided, it defaults to the last hour. Optionally narrow the search to a subset of streams with `matcher` (e.g. `{namespace="prod"}`).

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

endRfc3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now') (defaults to now)

matcher.description: Optionally, a stream selector to narrow the search to matching streams (Loki: LogQL, e.g. '{namespace="prod"}'; VictoriaLogs: LogsQL). Defaults to searching across all streams.

startRfc3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h') (defaults to 1 hour ago)

tools.name: list_loki_label_values
tools.description: Retrieves all unique values associated with a specific `labelName` within a Loki or VictoriaLogs datasource and time range. Returns a list of string values (e.g., for `labelName="env"`, might return `["prod", "staging", "dev"]`). Useful for discovering filter options. Defaults to the last hour if the time range is omitted. Optionally narrow the search to a subset of streams with `matcher` (e.g. `{namespace="prod"}`) вЂ” for example, to list `service` values seen only within a specific namespace.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

endRfc3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now') (defaults to now)

labelName.description: The name of the label to retrieve values for (e.g. 'app', 'env', 'pod')

matcher.description: Optionally, a stream selector to narrow the search to matching streams (Loki: LogQL, e.g. '{namespace="prod"}'; VictoriaLogs: LogsQL). Defaults to searching across all streams.

startRfc3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h') (defaults to 1 hour ago)

tools.name: list_oncall_schedules
tools.description: List Grafana OnCall schedules, optionally filtering by team ID. If a specific schedule ID is provided, retrieves details for only that schedule. Returns a list of schedule summaries including ID, name, team ID, timezone, and shift IDs. Supports pagination.

scheduleId.description: The ID of the schedule to get details for. If provided, returns only that schedule's details

teamId.description: The ID of the team to list schedules for

tools.name: list_oncall_teams
tools.description: List teams configured in Grafana OnCall. Returns a list of team objects with their details. Supports pagination.

tools.name: list_oncall_users
tools.description: List users from Grafana OnCall. These are OnCall users (separate from Grafana users). Can retrieve all users in the OnCall directory, a specific user by ID, or filter by username. Returns a list of user objects with their details. Supports pagination.

userId.description: The ID of the user to get details for. If provided, returns only that user's details

username.description: The username to filter users by. If provided, returns only the user matching this username

tools.name: list_prometheus_label_names
tools.description: List label names in a PromQL-compatible datasource (Prometheus, Thanos, Mimir, Cloud Monitoring, etc.). Allows filtering by series selectors and time range.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

endRfc3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the time range to filter the results by. Supports RFC3339 or relative time (e.g. 'now')

limit.description: Optionally, the maximum number of results to return

name.description: The name of the label to match against

value.description: The value to match against

type.description: One of the '=' or '!=' or '=~' or '!~'

matches.description: Optionally, a list of label matchers to filter the results by

projectName.description: GCP project name to query (Cloud Monitoring datasources only). Overrides or substitutes the defaultProject configured on the datasource.

startRfc3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the time range to filter the results by. Supports RFC3339 or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h')

tools.name: list_prometheus_label_values
tools.description: Use after list_prometheus_metric_names to find label values for filtering queries. Gets the values for a specific label name in a PromQL-compatible datasource (Prometheus, Thanos, Mimir, Cloud Monitoring, etc.). Allows filtering by series selectors and time range.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

endRfc3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the query. Supports RFC3339 or relative time (e.g. 'now')

labelName.description: The name of the label to query

limit.description: Optionally, the maximum number of results to return

name.description: The name of the label to match against

value.description: The value to match against

type.description: One of the '=' or '!=' or '=~' or '!~'

matches.description: Optionally, a list of selectors to filter the results by

projectName.description: GCP project name to query (Cloud Monitoring datasources only). Overrides or substitutes the defaultProject configured on the datasource.

startRfc3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query. Supports RFC3339 or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h')

tools.name: list_prometheus_metric_metadata
tools.description: List Prometheus metric metadata. Returns metadata about metrics currently scraped from targets. Note: This endpoint is experimental.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

limit.description: The maximum number of metrics to return

limitPerMetric.description: The maximum number of metrics to return per metric

projectName.description: GCP project name to query (Cloud Monitoring datasources only). Overrides or substitutes the defaultProject configured on the datasource.

tools.name: list_prometheus_metric_names
tools.description: DISCOVERY: Call this first to find available metrics before querying. Lists metric names in a PromQL-compatible datasource (Prometheus, Thanos, Mimir, Cloud Monitoring, etc.). Filters metric names using the provided regex. Supports pagination (page * limit must not exceed 10000) and an optional time range to restrict results to metrics active within that window. Cloud Monitoring ignores the time range.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

endRfc3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the time range to filter the results by. Supports RFC3339 or relative time (e.g. 'now')

limit.description: The maximum number of results to return

projectName.description: GCP project name to query (Cloud Monitoring datasources only). Overrides or substitutes the defaultProject configured on the datasource.

regex.description: The regex to match against the metric names

startRfc3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the time range to filter the results by. Supports RFC3339 or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h')

tools.name: list_provisioning_repositories
tools.description: List provisioning repositories (e.g. git-sync sources) configured for this Grafana instance. Returns each repository's slug along with its source URL, branch, path, sync state, and health. Use the returned `name` as the `repo` argument when rendering a not-yet-applied dashboard preview via get_panel_image's provisioningPreview parameter.

tools.name: list_pyroscope_label_names
tools.description:
Lists all available label names (keys) found in profiles within a specified Pyroscope datasource, time range, and
optional label matchers. Label matchers are typically used to qualify a service name ({service_name="foo"}). Returns a
list of unique label strings (e.g., ["app", "env", "pod"]). Label names with double underscores (e.g. __name__) are
internal and rarely useful to users. If the time range is not provided, it defaults to the last hour.

data_source_uid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

end_rfc_3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now') (defaults to now)

start_rfc_3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h') (defaults to 1 hour ago)

tools.name: list_pyroscope_label_values
tools.description:
Lists all available label values for a particular label name found in profiles within a specified Pyroscope datasource,
time range, and optional label matchers. Label matchers are typically used to qualify a service name ({service_name="foo"}).
Returns a list of unique label strings (e.g. for label name "env": ["dev", "staging", "prod"]). If the time range
is not provided, it defaults to the last hour.

data_source_uid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

end_rfc_3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now') (defaults to now)

matchers.description: Optionally, Prometheus style matchers used to filter the result set (defaults to: {})

start_rfc_3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h') (defaults to 1 hour ago)

tools.name: list_pyroscope_profile_types
tools.description:
Lists all available profile types available in a specified Pyroscope datasource and time range. Returns a list of all
available profile types (example profile type: "process_cpu:cpu:nanoseconds:cpu:nanoseconds"). A profile type has the
following structure: <name>:<sample type>:<sample unit>:<period type>:<period unit>. Not all profile types are available
for every service. If the time range is not provided, it defaults to the last hour.

data_source_uid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

end_rfc_3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now') (defaults to now)

start_rfc_3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h') (defaults to 1 hour ago)

tools.name: list_sift_investigations
tools.description: Retrieves a list of Sift investigations with an optional limit. If no limit is specified, defaults to 10 investigations.

limit.description: Maximum number of investigations to return

tools.name: list_snapshots
tools.description: List Grafana dashboard snapshots with optional query and result limit filters.

limit.description: Maximum number of snapshots to return (Grafana defaults to 1000 when omitted)

query.description: Optional search query for snapshot name

tools.name: list_tempo_attribute_names
tools.description: List available attribute names for TraceQL queries. Always pass a scope (resource, span, etc.) to avoid very large responses.

datasourceUid.description: UID of the tempo datasource to query

scope.description: Scope to filter attributes by (span, resource, event, link, instrumentation). Strongly recommended вЂ” omitting scope returns all attributes across all scopes which can be very large (100K+ chars).

tools.name: list_tempo_attribute_values
tools.description: List values for a fully scoped attribute name (e.g. resource.service.name). Useful for discovering what values exist for a specific attribute.

datasourceUid.description: UID of the tempo datasource to query

filter-query.description: Filter query to apply to the attribute values. It can only have one spanset and only &&'ed conditions like { <cond> && <cond> && ... }. This is useful for filtering the values to a specific set of values.

name.description: The attribute name to get values for (e.g. 'span.http.method', 'resource.service.name')

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

direction.description: Optionally, the direction of the query: 'forward' (oldest first) or 'backward' (newest first, default)

endRfc3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now')

format.description: Output format for log (streams) queries: 'full' (default) returns every entry with its own label metadata; 'compact' groups lines by stream so each label set is emitted only once, substantially reducing response size for broad queries. Structured metadata keys that are constant within a stream appear once on the stream header; keys that vary across lines appear per-line. Ignored for metric queries.

limit.description: Optionally, the maximum number of log lines to return (default max: 100, configurable by MCP server).

logql.description: The LogQL query to execute against Loki. This can be a simple label matcher or a complex query with filters, parsers, and expressions. Supports full LogQL syntax including label matchers, filter operators, pattern expressions, and pipeline operations.

queryType.description: Query type: 'range' (default) or 'instant'. Instant queries return a single value at one point in time. Range queries return values over a time window. Use 'instant' for metric queries when you want the current value.

startRfc3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h')

stepSeconds.description: Resolution step in seconds for range metric queries. When running metric queries with queryType='range', this controls the time resolution of the returned data points.

tools.name: query_loki_patterns
tools.description: Retrieves detected log patterns from a Loki datasource for a given stream selector and time range. Returns a list of patterns, each containing a pattern string and a total count of occurrences. Patterns help identify common log structures and anomalies. The `logql` parameter must be a stream selector (e.g., `{job="nginx"}`) and does not support line filters or aggregations. Defaults to the last hour if the time range is omitted. **Not supported on VictoriaLogs** datasources - use a `| stats` pipeline instead.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

endRfc3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now') (defaults to now)

logql.description: A LogQL stream selector to identify the logs to analyze for patterns (e.g. {job="foo", namespace="bar"})

startRfc3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h') (defaults to 1 hour ago)

tools.name: query_loki_stats
tools.description: Retrieves index-level statistics about log streams matching a given selector within a Loki or VictoriaLogs datasource and time range. Returns an object containing the count of streams, chunks, entries, and total bytes (e.g., `{"streams": 5, "chunks": 50, "entries": 10000, "bytes": 512000}`). **Important**: the `entries` count reflects storage-level index entries (chunk metadata), NOT the number of individual log lines matching the selector. To count actual matching log lines, use `query_loki_logs` with a `count_over_time()` metric query instead. On VictoriaLogs only `entries` is populated; the other fields remain zero. The `logql` parameter **must** be a simple label selector (e.g., `{app="nginx", env="prod"}`) and does not support line filters, parsers, or aggregations. Defaults to the last hour if the time range is omitted.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

endRfc3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now')

logql.description: The LogQL matcher expression to execute. This parameter only accepts label matcher expressions and does not support full LogQL queries. Line filters, pattern operations, and metric aggregations are not supported by the stats API endpoint. Only simple label selectors can be used here.

startRfc3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h')

tools.name: query_prometheus
tools.description: WORKFLOW: list_prometheus_metric_names -> list_prometheus_label_values -> query_prometheus. Query a PromQL-compatible datasource (Prometheus, Thanos, Mimir, Cloud Monitoring, etc.) using a PromQL expression. Supports instant queries (single point) and range queries (time range). Time: RFC3339 or relative expressions like 'now'\, 'now-1h'.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

endTime.description: The end time. Supported formats are RFC3339 or relative to now (e.g. 'now', 'now-1.5h', 'now-2h45m'). Valid time units are 'ns', 'us' (or 'Вµs'), 'ms', 's', 'm', 'h', 'd'.

projectName.description: GCP project name to query (Cloud Monitoring datasources only). Overrides or substitutes the defaultProject configured on the datasource.

queryType.description: The type of query to use. Either 'range' or 'instant'

startTime.description: The start time. Required if queryType is 'range', ignored if queryType is 'instant' Supported formats are RFC3339 or relative to now (e.g. 'now', 'now-1.5h', 'now-2h45m'). Valid time units are 'ns', 'us' (or 'Вµs'), 'ms', 's', 'm', 'h', 'd'.

stepSeconds.description: The time series step size in seconds. Required if queryType is 'range', ignored if queryType is 'instant'

tools.name: query_prometheus_histogram
tools.description:
Query Prometheus histogram percentiles. DISCOVER FIRST: Use list_prometheus_metric_names with regex='.*_bucket$' to find histograms.

Generates histogram_quantile PromQL. Example: metric='http_duration', percentile=95, labels='job="api"'

Time formats: 'now-1h', '2026-02-02T19:00:00Z', '1738519200000' (Unix ms)

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the Prometheus datasource

endTime.description: End time (default: now). Supports RFC3339, relative, or Unix ms.

projectName.description: GCP project name to query (Cloud Monitoring datasources only). Overrides or substitutes the defaultProject configured on the datasource.

startTime.description: Start time (default: now-1h). Supports RFC3339, relative (now-1h), or Unix ms.

stepSeconds.description: Step size in seconds for range query (default: 60)

tools.name: query_pyroscope
tools.description:
Unified Pyroscope query tool for fetching profiles or metrics from Pyroscope. Profile data shows WHICH functions consume resources; metrics data
shows WHEN consumption spiked. Use query_type="both" for complete analysis in one call.

query_type options (extends Grafana's PyroscopeQueryType):
- "profile": returns profile data (shape controlled by format)
- "metrics": returns time-series data points
- "both" (default): returns both profile and metrics in one response

format options (shape of the profile data):
- "table" (default): per-function table with flat (self) and cumulative values, ranked by flat
- "dot": call graph in Graphviz DOT format; nodes are per source line, so one function may span several nodes

data_source_uid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

end_rfc_3339.description: End time in RFC3339 or relative time (e.g. 'now') (defaults to now)

format.description: Profile output format: "table" (default) for a per-function flat/cum table, or "dot" for a call graph in Graphviz DOT format

group_by.description: Labels to group metrics series by

matchers.description: Prometheus style matchers (defaults to: {})

max_node_depth.description: Max functions in the profile table or nodes in the call graph; it is a count, not a depth (default: 100)

profile_type.description: The profile type, use list_pyroscope_profile_types to discover available types

query_type.description: Query type: "profile" (flamegraph), "metrics" (time-series), or "both" (default). Use "both" for complete analysis

start_rfc_3339.description: Start time in RFC3339 or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h') (defaults to 1 hour ago)

step.description: Seconds between metrics data points (default: auto)

tools.name: query_tempo_metrics
tools.description: Compute trace-derived metrics using a TraceQL metrics query. The syntax is unlike PromQL; call get_tempo_traceql_docs with topic 'metrics' for the reference. Use type 'instant' for a single value or 'range' for a time series (default). Instant queries over large time ranges may timeout вЂ” keep the window under 15 minutes for instant, or use range instead.

datasourceUid.description: UID of the tempo datasource to query

end.description: End time (RFC3339 format). If not provided will search the past 1 hour.

query.description: TraceQL metrics query of the form '{ <selector> } | <aggregation> [by (<attribute>)]'. Example: '{ } | quantile_over_time(span:duration, .99) by (span.name)'.

start.description: Start time (RFC3339 format). If not provided will search the past 1 hour.

type.description: Query type: 'instant' returns a single value at the end of the time range; 'range' returns a time series. Default is 'range'.

tools.name: search_dashboards
tools.description: Search Grafana dashboards by query and/or folderUid, tag, and starred. Returns matching dashboards with title, UID, folder, tags, and URL.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (max 100)

query.description: Optional query. Omit to filter by folderUid, tag, or starred

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search Grafana documentation. Returns matching pages with title, URL, description, and product. Call with no query to list available product groups.

limit.description: Maximum results to return (default 5)

product.description: Filter results to a specific product (e.g. 'Grafana Tempo', 'Grafana Loki')

query.description: Search query for Grafana documentation. Omit to list all available product groups.

tools.name: search_folders
tools.description: Search for Grafana folders by a query string. Returns matching folders with details like title, UID, and URL.

query.description: The query to search for

tools.name: search_plugin_information
tools.description: Search the Grafana plugin catalog by keyword to discover available plugins before installing or getting plugin details on a specific instance. Returns results sorted by trust: official Grafana Labs plugins first, then commercial partner plugins, then community plugins. Use this tool when a user describes a plugin by purpose or partial name (e.g. 'azure monitoring', 'loki', 'database') вЂ” it returns the exact pluginId to pass to get_plugin or install_plugin. Results include warnings for enterprise-only or Angular-based plugins.

query.description: Keyword to search for plugins (e.g. 'azure', 'prometheus', 'loki', 'database'). Matches against plugin name, slug, description, and keywords.

tools.name: search_tempo_traces
tools.description: Search for traces using TraceQL queries

datasourceUid.description: UID of the tempo datasource to query

end.description: End time for the search (RFC3339 format). If not provided will search the past 1 hour. If provided, must be after start.

query.description: TraceQL query string

Large dashboards consume significant context - consider using patches for small changes.

message.description: Set a commit message for the version history

Supports: '$.title', '$.panels[0].title', '$.panels[0].targets[0].expr', '$.panels[1].targets[0].datasource', '$.templating.list/-' (append a variable), '$.annotations.list/-' (append a saved dashboard annotation query/definition). For appending to arrays, use '/- ' syntax: '$.panels/- ' (append to panels array) or '$.panels[2]/- ' (append to nested array at index 2).

tools.name: update_datasource
tools.description: Update non-secret datasource fields by UID. Omitted fields are preserved. IMPORTANT: always call this tool twice. First call: provide only the uid вЂ” the tool returns the datasource's field schema. After receiving the schema, ask the user which fields they want to change and confirm each new value; do not infer or reset fields the user did not mention. Second call: provide the uid, schemaReviewed=true, and the changed values in the fields map. Returns an update message and a health check. For secrets, direct the user to the Grafana UI.

The server uses each field's target (root or jsonData) to place values correctly, merging jsonData changes into the existing settings. Only include the fields you want to change. Example: {"httpMethod": "POST"}.

tools.name: alerting_manage_routing
tools.description:
Manage Grafana alerting routing configuration, including notification policies, contact points and time intervals.

Notification policies define how alerts are grouped, routed, and which contact points receive them.
Time intervals define active/mute periods for alert notifications.

When to use:
- Understanding how alerts are routed to contact points/receivers
- Debugging why an alert went to a specific receiver
- Checking grouping, timing, or mute interval settings

When NOT to use:
- Checking alert rule configuration or state (use alerting_manage_rules)

contact_point_title.description: Title of the contact point to retrieve (required for get_contact_point operation)

datasource_uid.description: Optional: UID of an Alertmanager-compatible datasource to query for receivers. If omitted, returns Grafana-managed contact points. Only used with get_contact_points.

limit.description: The maximum number of results to return. Default is 100. Only used with get_contact_points.

name.description: Filter contact points by name (exact match). Only used with get_contact_points.

operation.description: The operation to perform: 'get_notification_policies' to retrieve the notification policy tree, 'get_contact_points' to list all contact points, 'get_contact_point' to get a specific contact point by name, 'get_time_intervals' to list all time intervals, 'get_time_interval' to get a specific time interval by name

time_interval_name.description: Name of the time interval to retrieve (required for get_time_interval operation)

tools.name: alerting_manage_rules
tools.description:
List and inspect Grafana alert rules with filtering capabilities.

When to use:
- Understanding why an alert is or isn't firing
- Auditing alert rule configuration (queries, conditions, labels, notification settings)
- Finding alert rules by state, folder, group, or name
- Comparing rule versions to see what changed

When NOT to use:
- Checking how alerts are routed to receivers (use alerting_manage_routing)
- Modifying or creating alert rules (read-only tool)

datasource_uid.description: Optional: UID of a Prometheus or Loki datasource to query for datasource-managed alert rules. If omitted, returns Grafana-managed rules.

folder_uid.description: Filter by exact folder UID (for 'list' operation). Mutually exclusive with search_folder.

label_selectors.description: Prometheus-style selectors to filter alert rules by labels. Each string is a selector e.g. '{severity="critical", team=~"backend.*"}'. All selectors must match (AND).

limit_alerts.description: Limit alert instances per rule. For list: 0 omits alerts. For get: <=0 defaults to 200. Max 200.

matchers.description: Label matchers to filter alert instances. Each string is a Prometheus-style matcher e.g. 'severity="critical"', 'env!="dev"', 'team=~"backend.*"'. Requires Grafana 12.4+.

operation.description: The operation to perform: 'list' to search/filter rules, 'get' to retrieve full rule details (state + configuration) by UID, or 'versions' to get the version history of a rule

rule_group.description: Filter by exact rule group name (for 'list' operation)

rule_limit.description: Maximum number of rules to return (default 200, max 200). Requires Grafana 12.4+ (for 'list' operation)

rule_uid.description: The UID of the alert rule (required for 'get' and 'versions' operations)

search_folder.description: Search folders by path using partial matching (for 'list' operation). Requires Grafana 12.4+. Mutually exclusive with folder_uid.

search_rule_name.description: Search alert rule names/titles using partial matching. Requires Grafana 12.4+ (for 'list' operation)

states.description: Filter by alert state: firing, pending, normal, recovering, nodata, error (for 'list' operation)

tools.name: alerting_manage_silences
tools.description:
List and inspect Grafana alerting silences. A silence temporarily suppresses notifications for alerts whose labels match a set of matchers.

Operations:
- 'list': list existing silences. Optionally filter by rule_uid (matches the __alert_rule_uid__ label) or by matchers.
- 'get': retrieve a single silence by silence_id.

When to use:
- Inspecting which alerts are currently silenced and why

When NOT to use:
- Creating, updating or deleting silences (read-only tool)
- Changing alert rule configuration or state (use alerting_manage_rules)
- Changing how alerts are routed to receivers (use alerting_manage_routing)

value.description: The label value to match against

isRegex.description: Whether value is a regular expression. Defaults to false.

isEqual.description: Whether the matcher asserts equality (true) or inequality (false). Defaults to true.

matchers.description: Optional label matchers used to filter listed silences. Only used with 'list'.

operation.description: The operation to perform: 'list' to list silences, 'get' to retrieve a silence by id

rule_uid.description: Optional: filter listed silences to those scoped to this alert rule UID (matches the __alert_rule_uid__ label). Only used with 'list'.

tools.name: get_dashboard_by_uid
tools.description: Retrieves the complete dashboard, including panels, variables, and settings, for a specific dashboard identified by its UID. Pass optional version to load a saved snapshot instead of the current dashboard. Saved snapshots are fetched through Grafana's legacy versions API, so 'apiVersion' is omitted and 'meta' is partial: only version, createdBy, and created are populated. For current (non-versioned) fetches, the response includes 'apiVersion' and 'isV2': when 'isV2' is true the dashboard uses the v2 schema (panels live under 'elements' keyed by name, arranged by 'layout'; variables under 'variables'), otherwise it is classic v1 ('panels[]' with 'templating.list'). WARNING: Large dashboards can consume significant context window space. Consider using get_dashboard_summary for overview or get_dashboard_property for specific data instead.

Returns an array of objects with fields: title, query (raw expression), datasource (object with uid and type), and optionally processedQuery, refId, requiredVariables, and target. Targets built in a visual editor (CloudWatch metric search, InfluxDB query builder) have no string expression: those return an empty query plus `target`, the panel's raw query JSON. Run those with run_panel_query rather than a query tool.

Classic v1 paths: '$.title' (title)\, '$.panels[*].title' (all panel titles)\, '$.panels[0]' (first panel)\, '$.templating.list' (variables)\, '$.annotations.list' (saved dashboard annotation queries/definitions)\, '$.tags' (tags)\, '$.panels[*].targets[*].expr' (all queries). v2 dashboards (see isV2 from get_dashboard_by_uid) use different paths: '$.title'\, '$.elements' (panels\, keyed by name)\, '$.variables' (variables)\, '$.annotations'. Use this instead of get_dashboard_by_uid when you only need specific dashboard properties.

tools.name: API-retrieve-page-markdown
tools.description:
Notion | Retrieve a page as Markdown
Error Responses:
400: Bad request
403: The integration lacks the read/update content capability required for this page.
404: Page not found or not shared with the integration.
429: Rate limited.

page_id.description: Identifier for a Notion page (or block) to read or update as markdown.

include_transcript.description: Whether to include meeting note transcripts. When false (default), a placeholder with the meeting note URL is shown instead of the full transcript.

tools.name: API-update-page-markdown
tools.description:
Notion | Update a page's content as Markdown
Error Responses:
400: Bad request
403: The integration lacks the read/update content capability required for this page.
404: Page not found or not shared with the integration.
409: Conflict (e.g. row limit exceeded).
429: Rate limited.

page_id.description: Identifier for a Notion page (or block) to read or update as markdown.

type.description: The kind of edit to apply. Prefer `replace_content` (overwrite the whole page) or `update_content` (targeted find-and-replace). `insert_content` and `replace_content_range` are deprecated.

anyOf.description: Provide when type is `replace_content`. Replaces the entire page content.

new_str.description: The complete new page content as enhanced Markdown.

allow_deleting_content.description: Permit deletion of existing child pages/databases that are no longer present in the new content.

anyOf.description: Provide when type is `update_content`. Applies targeted find-and-replace edits.

content_updates.description: Up to 100 find-and-replace edits applied in order.

old_str.description: Exact existing Markdown text to find.

new_str.description: Replacement Markdown text.

replace_all_matches.description: Replace every occurrence of old_str instead of just the first (default false).

allow_deleting_content.description: Permit deletion of existing child pages/databases removed by the edits.

anyOf.description: Deprecated. Provide when type is `insert_content`. Inserts Markdown at a position.

content.description: Enhanced Markdown to insert.

after.description: Ellipsis-format selection ("start text...end text") to insert after. Cannot be combined with position.

position.description: Insert at the start or end of the page. Cannot be combined with after.

anyOf.description: Deprecated. Provide when type is `replace_content_range`. Replaces a selected range of Markdown.

content.description: New Markdown content for the range.

content_range.description: Ellipsis-format selection ("start text...end text") identifying the range to replace.

allow_deleting_content.description: Permit deletion of child pages/databases within the replaced range.

tools.name: channels_list
tools.description: Get list of channels

channel_types.description: Comma-separated channel types. Allowed values: 'mpim', 'im', 'public_channel', 'private_channel'. Example: 'public_channel,private_channel,im'

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value of the last row and column in the response as next_cursor field returned from the previous request.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Must be an integer between 1 and 1000 (maximum 999).

query.description: Optional keyword to filter channels. Case-insensitive substring match against the fields specified by query_targets. Example: 'marketing' returns channels like #marketing, #marketing-ops.

query_targets.description: Comma-separated list of fields to match the query against. Allowed values: 'name', 'topic', 'purpose'. Example: 'name,topic,purpose' to search all fields. Default is 'name'.

sort.description: Type of sorting. Allowed values: 'popularity' - sort by number of members/participants in each channel.

tools.name: channels_me
tools.description: List channels you are a member of. Unlike channels_list which returns all workspace channels, this returns only channels you have joined. Useful on large workspaces where channels_list returns thousands of results.

channel_types.description: Comma-separated channel types. Allowed values: 'mpim', 'im', 'public_channel', 'private_channel'. Default: 'public_channel,private_channel'.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (1-999).

tools.name: conversations_history
tools.description: Get messages from the channel (or DM) by channel_id, the last row/column in the response is used as 'cursor' parameter for pagination if not empty

channel_id.description: - `channel_id` (string): ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... or @... aka #general or @username_dm.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value of the last row and column in the response as next_cursor field returned from the previous request.

include_activity_messages.description: If true, the response will include activity messages such as 'channel_join' or 'channel_leave'. Default is boolean false.

limit.description: Limit of messages to fetch in format of maximum ranges of time (e.g. 1d - 1 day, 1w - 1 week, 30d - 30 days, 90d - 90 days which is a default limit for free tier history) or number of messages (e.g. 50). Must be empty when 'cursor' is provided.

tools.name: conversations_join
tools.description: Join a public channel. Use channels_list or channels_me to find channel IDs.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... (e.g., #general).

tools.name: conversations_leave
tools.description: Leave a channel, group conversation, or DM. Cannot leave the #general channel.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... or @... (e.g., #general, @username).

tools.name: conversations_mark
tools.description: Mark a channel or DM as read. If no timestamp is provided, marks all messages as read.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... or @... (e.g., #general, @username).

ts.description: Timestamp of the message to mark as read up to. If not provided, marks all messages as read.

tools.name: conversations_replies
tools.description: Get a thread of messages posted to a conversation by channelID and thread_ts, the last row/column in the response is used as 'cursor' parameter for pagination if not empty

channel_id.description: ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... or @... aka #general or @username_dm.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value of the last row and column in the response as next_cursor field returned from the previous request.

include_activity_messages.description: If true, the response will include activity messages such as 'channel_join' or 'channel_leave'. Default is boolean false.

limit.description: Limit of messages to fetch in format of maximum ranges of time (e.g. 1d - 1 day, 30d - 30 days, 90d - 90 days which is a default limit for free tier history) or number of messages (e.g. 50). Must be empty when 'cursor' is provided.

thread_ts.description: Unique identifier of either a thread's parent message or a message in the thread. ts must be the timestamp in format 1234567890.123456 of an existing message with 0 or more replies.

tools.name: conversations_search_messages
tools.description: Search messages in a public channel, private channel, or direct message (DM, or IM) conversation using filters. All filters are optional, if not provided then search_query is required.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value of the last row and column in the response as next_cursor field returned from the previous request.

filter_date_after.description: Filter messages sent after a specific date in format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Example: '2023-10-01', 'July', 'Yesterday' or 'Today'. If not provided, all dates will be searched.

filter_date_before.description: Filter messages sent before a specific date in format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Example: '2023-10-01', 'July', 'Yesterday' or 'Today'. If not provided, all dates will be searched.

filter_date_during.description: Filter messages sent during a specific period in format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Example: 'July', 'Yesterday' or 'Today'. If not provided, all dates will be searched.

filter_date_on.description: Filter messages sent on a specific date in format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Example: '2023-10-01', 'July', 'Yesterday' or 'Today'. If not provided, all dates will be searched.

filter_in_channel.description: Filter messages in a specific public/private channel by its ID or name. Example: 'C1234567890', 'G1234567890', or '#general'. If not provided, all channels will be searched.

filter_in_im_or_mpim.description: Filter messages in a direct message (DM) or multi-person direct message (MPIM) conversation by its ID or name. Example: 'D1234567890' or '@username_dm'. If not provided, all DMs and MPIMs will be searched.

filter_threads_only.description: If true, the response will include only messages from threads. Default is boolean false.

filter_users_from.description: Filter messages from a specific user by their ID or display name. Example: 'U1234567890' or '@username'. If not provided, all users will be searched.

filter_users_with.description: Filter messages with a specific user by their ID or display name in threads and DMs. Example: 'U1234567890' or '@username'. If not provided, all threads and DMs will be searched.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Must be an integer between 1 and 100.

search_query.description: Search query to filter messages. Example: 'marketing report' or full URL of Slack message e.g. 'https://slack.com/archives/C1234567890/p1234567890123456', then the tool will return a single message matching given URL, herewith all other parameters will be ignored.

tools.name: conversations_unreads
tools.description: Get unread messages across all channels. With browser session tokens (xoxc/xoxd), uses a single API call for complete results. channel_types.description: Filter by channel type: 'all' (default), 'dm' (direct messages), 'group_dm' (group DMs), 'partner' (ext-* channels), 'internal' (other channels).

include_messages.description: If true (default), returns the actual unread messages. If false, returns only a summary of channels with unreads.

include_muted.description: If true, includes muted channels in results. Default is false (muted channels are excluded, matching Slack app behavior).

max_channels.description: Maximum number of channels to fetch unreads from. Default is 50.

max_messages_per_channel.description: Maximum messages to fetch per channel. Default is 10.

mentions_only.description: If true, only returns channels where you have @mentions. Default is false.

tools.name: usergroups_create

channels.description: Comma-separated channel IDs where this group is commonly mentioned. Members get suggestions to join these channels.

description.description: Purpose or description shown in group details (e.g., 'Backend and frontend engineers').

handle.description: The @mention handle without the @ symbol (e.g., 'engineering' for @engineering). Keep it short and lowercase. If omitted, Slack auto-generates one from the name.

name.description: Display name of the user group (e.g., 'Engineering Team', 'Design Squad').

include_disabled.description: Include disabled/archived groups. Default is false.

tools.name: usergroups_update

channels.description: New default channel IDs (comma-separated). Replaces existing default channels.

handle.description: New @mention handle (without @). Changing this changes how users mention the group.

name.description: New display name for the group.

usergroup_id.description: ID of the user group to update (starts with 'S', e.g., 'S0123456789'). Get IDs from usergroups_list.

tools.name: usergroups_users_update
tools.description: Replace all members of a user group with a new list. WARNING: This completely replaces the member list - any user not in the 'users' parameter will be removed. usergroup_id.description: ID of the user group (starts with 'S', e.g., 'S0123456789'). Get IDs from usergroups_list.

users.description: Comma-separated user IDs that will become the COMPLETE member list (e.g., 'U0123456789,U9876543210'). All current members not in this list will be removed.

tools.name: channels_list

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value of the last row and column in the response as next_cursor field returned from the previous request.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Must be an integer between 1 and 1000 (maximum 999).

query.description: Optional keyword to filter channels. Case-insensitive substring match against the fields specified by query_targets. Example: 'marketing' returns channels like #marketing, #marketing-ops.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value of the last row and column in the response as next_cursor field returned from the previous request.

include_activity_messages.description: If true, the response will include activity messages such as 'channel_join' or 'channel_leave'. Default is boolean false.

limit.description: Limit of messages to fetch in format of maximum ranges of time (e.g. 1d - 1 day, 1w - 1 week, 30d - 30 days, 90d - 90 days which is a default limit for free tier history) or number of messages (e.g. 50). Must be empty when 'cursor' is provided.

tools.name: conversations_replies

channel_id.description: ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... or @... aka #general or @username_dm.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value of the last row and column in the response as next_cursor field returned from the previous request.

include_activity_messages.description: If true, the response will include activity messages such as 'channel_join' or 'channel_leave'. Default is boolean false.

limit.description: Limit of messages to fetch in format of maximum ranges of time (e.g. 1d - 1 day, 30d - 30 days, 90d - 90 days which is a default limit for free tier history) or number of messages (e.g. 50). Must be empty when 'cursor' is provided.

tools.name: conversations_search_messages
tools.description: Search messages in a public channel, private channel, or direct message (DM, or IM) conversation using filters. All filters are optional, if not provided then search_query is required.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value of the last row and column in the response as next_cursor field returned from the previous request.

filter_date_after.description: Filter messages sent after a specific date in format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Example: '2023-10-01', 'July', 'Yesterday' or 'Today'. If not provided, all dates will be searched.

filter_date_before.description: Filter messages sent before a specific date in format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Example: '2023-10-01', 'July', 'Yesterday' or 'Today'. If not provided, all dates will be searched.

filter_date_during.description: Filter messages sent during a specific period in format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Example: 'July', 'Yesterday' or 'Today'. If not provided, all dates will be searched.

filter_date_on.description: Filter messages sent on a specific date in format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Example: '2023-10-01', 'July', 'Yesterday' or 'Today'. If not provided, all dates will be searched.

filter_in_channel.description: Filter messages in a specific public/private channel by its ID or name. Example: 'C1234567890', 'G1234567890', or '#general'. If not provided, all channels will be searched.

filter_in_im_or_mpim.description: Filter messages in a direct message (DM) or multi-person direct message (MPIM) conversation by its ID or name. Example: 'D1234567890' or '@username_dm'. If not provided, all DMs and MPIMs will be searched.

filter_threads_only.description: If true, the response will include only messages from threads. Default is boolean false.

filter_users_from.description: Filter messages from a specific user by their ID or display name. Example: 'U1234567890' or '@username'. If not provided, all users will be searched.

filter_users_with.description: Filter messages with a specific user by their ID or display name in threads and DMs. Example: 'U1234567890' or '@username'. If not provided, all threads and DMs will be searched.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Must be an integer between 1 and 100.

search_query.description: Search query to filter messages. Example: 'marketing report' or full URL of Slack message e.g. 'https://slack.com/archives/C1234567890/p1234567890123456', then the tool will return a single message matching given URL, herewith all other parameters will be ignored.

tools.name: conversations_unreads
tools.description: Get unread messages across all channels. With browser session tokens (xoxc/xoxd), uses a single API call for complete results. With OAuth user tokens (xoxp), scans a subset of channels per type (limited by max_channels) Р В Р вЂ Р В РІР‚С™Р Р†Р вЂљРЎСљ results may be partial on large workspaces. Results are prioritized: DMs > group DMs > partner channels > internal channels.

channel_types.description: Filter by channel type: 'all' (default), 'dm' (direct messages), 'group_dm' (group DMs), 'partner' (ext-* channels), 'internal' (other channels).

include_messages.description: If true (default), returns the actual unread messages. If false, returns only a summary of channels with unreads.

include_muted.description: If true, includes muted channels in results. Default is false (muted channels are excluded, matching Slack app behavior).

max_channels.description: Maximum number of channels to fetch unreads from. Default is 50.

max_messages_per_channel.description: Maximum messages to fetch per channel. Default is 10.

mentions_only.description: If true, only returns channels where you have @mentions. Default is false.

tools.name: usergroups_create
tools.description: Create a new user group (mention group) in the Slack workspace. After creation, use usergroups_users_update to add members, or users can join themselves with usergroups_me. The handle becomes the @mention (e.g., handle='engineering' creates @engineering).

channels.description: Comma-separated channel IDs where this group is commonly mentioned. Members get suggestions to join these channels.

description.description: Purpose or description shown in group details (e.g., 'Backend and frontend engineers').

handle.description: The @mention handle without the @ symbol (e.g., 'engineering' for @engineering). Keep it short and lowercase. If omitted, Slack auto-generates one from the name.

name.description: Display name of the user group (e.g., 'Engineering Team', 'Design Squad').

tools.name: usergroups_list
tools.description: List all user groups (subteams) in the Slack workspace. User groups are mention groups like @engineering or @design that notify all members. Use this to discover available groups, check group membership counts, or find a group's ID before joining/updating it. Returns CSV with columns: id, name, handle, description, user_count, is_external.

include_count.description: Include user count for each group. Default is true.

include_disabled.description: Include disabled/archived groups. Default is false.

include_users.description: Include list of user IDs in each group. Default is false.

tools.name: usergroups_me
tools.description: Manage your own user group membership. Use action='list' to see which groups you belong to. Use action='join' with a usergroup_id to add yourself to a group (e.g., to receive @mentions). Use action='leave' with a usergroup_id to remove yourself. This is the easiest way to join/leave groups without needing to know the full member list.

action.description: Action to perform: 'list' returns CSV of groups you're a member of, 'join' adds you to a group, 'leave' removes you from a group.

usergroup_id.description: ID of the user group (starts with 'S', e.g., 'S0123456789'). Required for 'join' and 'leave' actions. Get IDs from usergroups_list.

tools.name: usergroups_update
tools.description: Update a user group's metadata: name, handle (@mention), description, or default channels. Does NOT change members - use usergroups_users_update for that. At least one field must be provided.

channels.description: New default channel IDs (comma-separated). Replaces existing default channels.

handle.description: New @mention handle (without @). Changing this changes how users mention the group.

name.description: New display name for the group.

usergroup_id.description: ID of the user group to update (starts with 'S', e.g., 'S0123456789'). Get IDs from usergroups_list.

tools.name: usergroups_users_update
tools.description: Replace all members of a user group with a new list. WARNING: This completely replaces the member list - any user not in the 'users' parameter will be removed. To add/remove just yourself, use usergroups_me instead. To add a single user without removing others, first get current members from usergroups_list with include_users=true, then call this with the combined list.

usergroup_id.description: ID of the user group (starts with 'S', e.g., 'S0123456789'). Get IDs from usergroups_list.

users.description: Comma-separated user IDs that will become the COMPLETE member list (e.g., 'U0123456789,U9876543210'). All current members not in this list will be removed.
