tools.name: alerting_manage_routing
tools.description:
Manage Grafana alerting routing configuration, including notification policies, contact points and time intervals.

Notification policies define how alerts are grouped, routed, and which contact points receive them.
Time intervals define active/mute periods for alert notifications.

When to use:
- Understanding how alerts are routed to contact points/receivers
- Debugging why an alert went to a specific receiver
- Checking grouping, timing, or mute interval settings

When NOT to use:
- Checking alert rule configuration or state (use alerting_manage_rules)

contact_point_title.description: Title of the contact point to retrieve (required for get_contact_point operation)

datasource_uid.description: Optional: UID of an Alertmanager-compatible datasource to query for receivers. If omitted, returns Grafana-managed contact points. Only used with get_contact_points.

limit.description: The maximum number of results to return. Default is 100. Only used with get_contact_points.

name.description: Filter contact points by name (exact match). Only used with get_contact_points.

operation.description: The operation to perform: 'get_notification_policies' to retrieve the notification policy tree, 'get_contact_points' to list all contact points, 'get_contact_point' to get a specific contact point by name, 'get_time_intervals' to list all time intervals, 'get_time_interval' to get a specific time interval by name

time_interval_name.description: Name of the time interval to retrieve (required for get_time_interval operation)

tools.name: alerting_manage_rules
tools.description:
Manage Grafana alert rules with full CRUD capabilities and filtering.

When to use:
- Understanding why an alert is or isn't firing
- Auditing alert rule configuration (queries, conditions, labels, notification settings)
- Finding alert rules by state, folder, group, or name
- Creating, updating, or deleting alert rules
- Comparing rule versions to see what changed

When NOT to use:
- Checking how alerts are routed to receivers (use alerting_manage_routing)

annotations.description: Optional annotations for the alert rule

condition.description: The query condition identifier, e.g. 'A', 'B' (required for 'create', 'update')

data.description: Array of alert query objects (required for 'create'/'update'). Each object has: datasourceUid (string, required), model (object with expr for data queries or type/expression/conditions for expressions), refId (string, auto-assigned if omitted), relativeTimeRange ({from, to} in seconds, defaults to {from:600,to:0}). For server-side expressions use datasourceUid '__expr__'. Example: [{datasourceUid: 'prometheus', model: {expr: 'up == 0'}}, {datasourceUid: '__expr__', model: {type: 'threshold', expression: 'A', conditions: [{evaluator: {type: 'gt', params: [0]}}]}}]

datasource_uid.description: Optional: UID of a Prometheus or Loki datasource to query for datasource-managed alert rules (for 'list' operation)

disable_provenance.description: If true, the alert remains editable in the Grafana UI (sets X-Disable-Provenance header). Defaults to true.

exec_err_state.description: State on execution error: NoData, Alerting, OK (required for 'create', 'update')

folder_uid.description: The folder UID. For 'list': filter by exact folder UID (mutually exclusive with search_folder). For 'create'/'update': the folder to store the rule in (required).

for.description: Duration before alert fires, e.g. '5m' (required for 'create', 'update')

is_paused.description: If true, the alert rule remains inactive, Default is false

keep_firing_for.description: Enables continous firing of alert for specified time even when condition is no longer met. Default is 0 (resolves immediately)

label_selectors.description: Prometheus-style selectors to filter alert rules by labels. Each string is a selector e.g. '{severity="critical", team=~"backend.*"}'. All selectors must match (AND).

labels.description: Optional labels for the alert rule

limit_alerts.description: Limit alert instances per rule. For list: 0 omits alerts. For get: <=0 defaults to 200. Max 200.

matchers.description: Label matchers to filter alert instances. Each string is a Prometheus-style matcher e.g. 'severity="critical"', 'env!="dev"', 'team=~"backend.*"'. Requires Grafana 12.4+.

missing_series_evals_to_resolve.description: Consecutive evaluation intervals with no data required to mark the alert as resolved. Default is 2.

no_data_state.description: State when no data: NoData, Alerting, OK (required for 'create', 'update')

notification_settings.description: Notification settings object. Fields: receiver (string, required), groupBy ([]string), groupWait/groupInterval/repeatInterval (duration strings), muteTimeIntervals/activeTimeIntervals ([]string).

operation.description: The operation to perform: 'list', 'get', 'versions', 'create', 'update', or 'delete'. To create a rule, use operation 'create' and provide all required fields in a single call. To update a rule, first use 'get' to retrieve its full configuration, then 'update' with all required fields plus your changes.

record.description: Recording rule config. Fields: from (string, required - ref ID e.g. 'A'), metric (string, required - metric name), targetDatasourceUid (string, optional).

rule_limit.description: Maximum number of rules to return (default 200, max 200). Requires Grafana 12.4+ (for 'list' operation)

rule_uid.description: The UID of the alert rule (required for 'get', 'versions', 'update', 'delete'; optional for 'create')

search_folder.description: Search folders by path using partial matching (for 'list' operation). Requires Grafana 12.4+. Mutually exclusive with folder_uid.

search_rule_name.description: Search alert rule names/titles using partial matching. Requires Grafana 12.4+ (for 'list' operation)

states.description: Filter by alert state: firing, pending, normal, recovering, nodata, error (for 'list' operation)

title.description: The title of the alert rule (required for 'create', 'update')

comment.description: A human-readable comment explaining the silence (required for 'create' and 'update')

created_by.description: Author of the silence. Defaults to 'grafana-assistant'.

ends_at.description: Silence end time in RFC3339 format, e.g. '2026-07-11T12:00:00Z' (required for 'create' and 'update')

value.description: The label value to match against

isRegex.description: Whether value is a regular expression. Defaults to false.

isEqual.description: Whether the matcher asserts equality (true) or inequality (false). Defaults to true.

matchers.description: Label matchers. Required (at least one) for 'create' and 'update'. For 'list', used as an optional filter.

operation.description: The operation to perform: 'list' to list silences, 'get' to retrieve a silence by id, 'create' to create a new silence, 'update' to modify an existing silence by id, 'delete' to expire a silence by id

rule_uid.description: Optional: filter listed silences to those scoped to this alert rule UID (matches the __alert_rule_uid__ label). Only used with 'list'.

starts_at.description: Silence start time in RFC3339 format, e.g. '2026-07-11T10:00:00Z' (required for 'create' and 'update'). Grafana clamps a start time in the past to the moment of creation, so for 'update' pass back the starts_at returned by 'get' to keep the silence id stable.

tools.name: analyze_loki_labels
tools.description: Audits a Loki label strategy and optionally diagnoses query performance. Returns per-label verdicts, missing base labels, normalisation issues, and a recommended set. Pass datasourceUid for live cardinality or labels for static scoring; both may be combined.

datasourceUid.description: Datasource UID (live mode).

perfMetrics.description: Runtime metrics; presence triggers perf diagnosis.

selector.description: Optional LogQL selector for stats / perf diagnosis.

tools.name: check_datasources_health
tools.description: Check datasource health. Filter by type or UIDs; omit both to check all.

type.description: Plugin type filter; omit to check all

tools.name: create_annotation
tools.description: Create a new annotation on a dashboard or panel. Set format to 'graphite' and provide 'what' for Graphite-format annotations.

dashboardUid.description: Dashboard UID

format.description: Set to 'graphite' to create a Graphite-format annotation

graphiteData.description: Optional string payload for Graphite format

text.description: Annotation text (required unless format is graphite)

what.description: Annotation text for Graphite format (required when format is graphite)

when.description: Epoch ms timestamp for Graphite format

tools.name: create_datasource
tools.description: Create a datasource. If type is ambiguous, call search_plugin_information first; install the plugin if needed. IMPORTANT: always call this tool twice. First call: provide only the type Р В Р вЂ Р В РІР‚С™Р Р†Р вЂљРЎСљ the tool returns a field schema. After receiving the schema, you MUST ask the user for every required field value explicitly; do not infer or use defaults without user confirmation. Second call: provide the type, the display name in the top-level name argument, schemaReviewed=true, and the fields map populated with values confirmed by the user. Never handle credentials Р В Р вЂ Р В РІР‚С™Р Р†Р вЂљРЎСљ remind the user to rotate any detected. Returns UID, health check, and a config page link.

access.description: How Grafana should access the datasource (proxy or direct)

basicAuth.description: Whether Grafana should use basic auth

fields.description: Datasource field values to provision, keyed by field key from the schema returned on the first call. The server uses each field's target (root or jsonData) to place values correctly in the YAML. Example: {"url": "http://prometheus:9090", "httpMethod": "POST"}.

isDefault.description: Whether this should become the default datasource

schemaReviewed.description: Set to true on the second call to confirm you reviewed the schema and collected values from the user.

type.description: Grafana datasource plugin type, for example prometheus

url.description: Datasource base URL when required by the plugin

withCredentials.description: Whether Grafana should forward credentials such as cookies

tools.name: create_folder
tools.description: Create a Grafana folder. Provide a title and optional UID. Returns the created folder.

parentUid.description: Optional parent folder UID. If set, the folder will be created under this parent.

uid.description: Optional folder UID. If omitted, Grafana will generate one.

tools.name: create_incident
tools.description: Create a new Grafana incident. Requires title, severity, and room prefix. Allows setting status, labels and custom fields. This tool should be used judiciously and sparingly, and only after confirmation from the user, as it may notify or alarm lots of people.

field.description: The name or UUID of the custom field to set. Use list_incident_custom_fields to discover the available fields

values.description: The value(s) to set. Text and number fields take a single value; single-select fields take one option; multi-select fields take one or more options. Select options may be given as their label, value or UUID. Pass an empty list to clear the field

customFields.description: Custom field values to set on the new incident. Use list_incident_custom_fields to discover the available fields and their valid values

isDrill.description: Whether the incident is a drill incident

labels.description: The labels to add to the incident

roomPrefix.description: The prefix of the room to create the incident in

status.description: The status of the incident

tools.name: create_snapshot
tools.description: Create a Grafana snapshot from a full dashboard payload. Supports optional expiration and external snapshot fields.

dashboard.description: Complete dashboard model to snapshot (as returned by Grafana dashboard APIs)

deleteKey.description: Secret key for deleting external snapshots. Required when external is true

expires.description: Snapshot expiration in seconds (e.g. 3600 for 1 hour)

external.description: Store snapshot on external server. Requires key and deleteKey when true

key.description: Custom snapshot key. Required when external is true

tools.name: delete_annotation
tools.description: Permanently delete an annotation by ID. The annotation cannot be recovered afterwards.

id.description: Annotation ID to delete

tools.name: delete_snapshot
tools.description: Delete a Grafana snapshot by snapshot key.

tools.name: diff_tempo_traces
tools.description: Compare two complete traces. Returns a compact summary and includes the full span-level patch when it is at most 64 KiB. Request trace-patch-v0 only when full details are required; full patches are not size-bounded.

base_end.description: Optional end of the baseline trace search range in RFC3339 format. Must be provided with base_start.

base_start.description: Optional start of the baseline trace search range in RFC3339 format. Must be provided with base_end.

base_trace_id.description: Trace ID for the baseline trace

compare_end.description: Optional end of the comparison trace search range in RFC3339 format. Must be provided with compare_start.

compare_start.description: Optional start of the comparison trace search range in RFC3339 format. Must be provided with compare_end.

compare_trace_id.description: Trace ID for the comparison trace

datasourceUid.description: UID of the tempo datasource to query

format.description: Output format. The composed format returns a compact summary and attaches the full patch only when it is at most 64 KiB. trace-patch-v0 has no output-size guarantee.

tools.name: find_error_pattern_logs
tools.description: Searches Loki logs for elevated error patterns compared to the last day's average, waits for the analysis to complete, and returns the results including any patterns found. Use the labelSelector parameter with PromQL/LogQL syntax for pattern matching on label values (e.g. {namespace=~"prod.*"}).

end.description: End time for the investigation. Defaults to now if not specified.

labelSelector.description: A PromQL/LogQL stream selector to scope the analysis. Supports all match operators: = (exact), != (not equal), =~ (regex), !~ (negative regex). Example: {namespace=~"prod.*", cluster="us-east-1"}

start.description: Start time for the investigation. Defaults to 30 minutes ago if not specified.

tools.name: find_slow_requests
tools.description: Searches relevant Tempo datasources for slow requests, waits for the analysis to complete, and returns the results. Use the labelSelector parameter with PromQL/LogQL syntax for pattern matching on label values (e.g. {namespace=~"prod.*"}).

end.description: End time for the investigation. Defaults to now if not specified.

labelSelector.description: A PromQL/LogQL stream selector to scope the analysis. Supports all match operators: = (exact), != (not equal), =~ (regex), !~ (negative regex). Example: {namespace=~"prod.*", cluster="us-east-1"}

start.description: Start time for the investigation. Defaults to 30 minutes ago if not specified.

tools.name: generate_deeplink
tools.description: Generate deeplink URLs for Grafana resources. Supports dashboards (requires dashboardUid or provisioningPreview), panels (requires dashboardUid or provisioningPreview, plus panelId), and Explore queries (requires datasourceUid and optionally queries). For dashboard and panel links, provisioningPreview points at a dashboard staged on a provisioning repository branch (e.g. a git-sync PR preview). For explore links, the time range and queries are embedded inside the Grafana explore state. Set shorten=true to also attempt a /goto/<uid> short URL; if shortening fails, the full deeplink is returned.

dashboardUid.description: Dashboard UID (for stored dashboards). Mutually exclusive with provisioningPreview for dashboard and panel types.

datasourceUid.description: Datasource UID (required for explore type)

repo.description: Provisioning repository slug. List repositories via list_provisioning_repositories if unknown.

pullRequestUrl.description: Upstream pull request URL to surface in Grafana's preview banner.

provisioningPreview.description: Identifies a dashboard staged on a provisioning repository branch (e.g. a git-sync PR preview). Mutually exclusive with dashboardUid for dashboard and panel types.

queries.description: List of query objects for explore links (e.g. [{"refId":"A","expr":"up"}])

queryParams.description: Additional URL query parameters (for dashboard/panel types)

resourceType.description: Type of resource: dashboard, panel, or explore

shorten.description: If true, try to shorten the generated URL to /goto/<uid>. If shortening fails, return the original deeplink.

tools.name: get_alert_group
tools.description: Get a specific alert group from Grafana OnCall by its ID. Returns the full alert group details, including the most recent alert and its raw payload when the OnCall API provides them. Alert payloads carry integration-specific fingerprints (for example Sentry's payload.data.event.hashes or Alertmanager's payload.alerts[].fingerprint) that identify recurring alerts across different alert groups.

alertGroupId.description: The ID of the alert group to retrieve

tools.name: get_annotation_tags
tools.description: Returns annotation tags with optional filtering by tag name. Only the provided filters are applied.

limit.description: Max results, default 100

tools.name: get_annotations
tools.description: Fetch Grafana annotations using filters such as dashboard UID, time range and tags.

dashboardUid.description: Filter by dashboard UID

limit.description: Max results default 100

matchAny.description: If true, match any tag (OR). If false, match all tags (AND). Default: false

type.description: annotation or alert

tools.name: get_assertions
tools.description: Get assertion summary for a given entity with its type, name, env, site, namespace, and a time range

endTime.description: The end time in RFC3339 format (e.g. 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z) or relative format (e.g. now)

entityName.description: The name of the entity to list

entityType.description: The type of the entity to list (e.g. Service, Node, Pod, etc.)

namespace.description: The namespace of the entity to list

site.description: The site of the entity to list

startTime.description: The start time in RFC3339 format (e.g. 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z) or relative format (e.g. now-1h)

tools.name: get_current_oncall_users
tools.description: Get the list of users currently on-call for a specific Grafana OnCall schedule ID. Returns the schedule ID, name, and a list of detailed user objects for those currently on call.

scheduleId.description: The ID of the schedule to get current on-call users for

tools.name: get_dashboard_by_uid
tools.description: Retrieves the complete dashboard, including panels, variables, and settings, for a specific dashboard identified by its UID. Pass optional version to load a saved snapshot instead of the current dashboard. Saved snapshots are fetched through Grafana's legacy versions API, so 'apiVersion' is omitted and 'meta' is partial: only version, createdBy, and created are populated. For current (non-versioned) fetches, the response includes 'apiVersion' and 'isV2': when 'isV2' is true the dashboard uses the v2 schema (panels live under 'elements' keyed by name, arranged by 'layout'; variables under 'variables'), otherwise it is classic v1 ('panels[]' with 'templating.list'). WARNING: Large dashboards can consume significant context window space. Consider using get_dashboard_summary for overview or get_dashboard_property for specific data instead.

version.description: Optional saved version. Omit for the current dashboard

tools.name: get_dashboard_panel_queries
tools.description: Retrieve panel queries from a Grafana dashboard. Supports all datasource types (Prometheus, Loki, CloudWatch, SQL, etc.) and row-nested panels. Optionally filter to a specific panel by ID with `panelId`. Optionally provide `variables` for template variable substitution, which populates `processedQuery` and `requiredVariables` fields. Returns an array of objects with fields: title, query (raw expression), datasource (object with uid and type), and optionally processedQuery, refId, requiredVariables, and target. Targets built in a visual editor (CloudWatch metric search, InfluxDB query builder) have no string expression: those return an empty query plus `target`, the panel's raw query JSON. Run those with run_panel_query rather than a query tool.

panelId.description: Optional panel ID to filter to a specific panel

tools.name: get_dashboard_property
tools.description: Get specific parts of a dashboard using JSONPath expressions to minimize context window usage. JSONPath targets the dashboard's native schema. Classic v1 paths: '$.title' (title)\, '$.panels[*].title' (all panel titles)\, '$.panels[0]' (first panel)\, '$.templating.list' (variables)\, '$.annotations.list' (saved dashboard annotation queries/definitions)\, '$.tags' (tags)\, '$.panels[*].targets[*].expr' (all queries). v2 dashboards (see isV2 from get_dashboard_by_uid) use different paths: '$.title'\, '$.elements' (panels\, keyed by name)\, '$.variables' (variables)\, '$.annotations'. Use this instead of get_dashboard_by_uid when you only need specific dashboard properties.

jsonPath.description: JSONPath expression to extract specific data (e.g., '$.panels[0].title' for first panel title, '$.panels[*].title' for all panel titles, '$.templating.list' for variables, '$.annotations.list' for saved dashboard annotation queries/definitions)

tools.name: get_dashboard_summary

tools.name: get_datasource

uid.description: The UID of the datasource. If provided, takes priority over name.

tools.name: get_doc

tools.name: get_incident

tools.name: get_oncall_shift

tools.name: get_panel_image

Either dashboardUid (for stored dashboards) or provisioningPreview (for dashboards staged on a provisioning repository branch, e.g. a git-sync PR) must be supplied. Use this for generating visual snapshots of dashboards for reports, alerts, or presentations.

dashboardUid.description: The UID of a stored dashboard containing the panel. Required unless provisioningPreview is provided.

height.description: Height of the rendered image in pixels. Defaults to 500

panelId.description: The ID of the panel to render. If omitted, the entire dashboard is rendered

repo.description: Provisioning repository slug. List repositories via /apis/provisioning.grafana.app/v0alpha1/namespaces/default/repositories if unknown.

path.description: Path to the dashboard file within the repository, relative to its root.

ref.description: Branch or commit SHA to render from. Defaults to the repository's main branch when omitted.

timeRange.description: Time range for the rendered image

width.description: Width of the rendered image in pixels. Defaults to 1000

tools.name: get_plugin
tools.description: Check whether a Grafana plugin is installed and retrieve its details (name, version, type, enabled status). Returns installed=false when the plugin is not found. Use install_plugin when a plugin is not installed to install plugin after confirming this action with the user.

tools.name: get_sift_analysis

tools.name: get_sift_investigation

tools.name: get_snapshot

tools.description: Retrieve a specific trace by ID

tools.name: grafana_api_request

tools.name: install_plugin

tools.name: list_alert_groups

tools.name: list_datasources

matcher.description: Optionally, a stream selector to narrow the search to matching streams (Loki: LogQL, e.g. '{namespace="prod"}'; VictoriaLogs: LogsQL). Defaults to searching across all streams.

startRfc3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h') (defaults to 1 hour ago)

tools.name: list_prometheus_label_values

To count actual matching log lines, use `query_loki_logs` with a `count_over_time()` metric query instead. On VictoriaLogs only `entries` is populated; the other fields remain zero. The `logql` parameter **must** be a simple label selector (e.g., `{app="nginx", env="prod"}`) and does not support line filters, parsers, or aggregations. query_type options (extends Grafana's PyroscopeQueryType):
- "profile": returns profile data (shape controlled by format)
- "metrics": returns time-series data points
- "both" (default): returns both profile and metrics in one response

format options (shape of the profile data):
- "table" (default): per-function table with flat (self) and cumulative values, ranked by flat
- "dot": call graph in Graphviz DOT format; nodes are per source line, so one function may span several nodes

query_type.description: Query type: "profile" (flamegraph), "metrics" (time-series), or "both" (default). Use "both" for complete analysis

tools.name: channels_list
tools.description: Get list of channels

channel_types.description: Comma-separated channel types. Allowed values: 'mpim', 'im', 'public_channel', 'private_channel'. Example: 'public_channel,private_channel,im'

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value of the last row and column in the response as next_cursor field returned from the previous request.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Must be an integer between 1 and 1000 (maximum 999).

query.description: Optional keyword to filter channels. Case-insensitive substring match against the fields specified by query_targets. Example: 'marketing' returns channels like #marketing, #marketing-ops.

query_targets.description: Comma-separated list of fields to match the query against. Allowed values: 'name', 'topic', 'purpose'. Example: 'name,topic,purpose' to search all fields. Default is 'name'.

sort.description: Type of sorting. Allowed values: 'popularity' - sort by number of members/participants in each channel.

tools.name: channels_me
tools.description: List channels you are a member of. Unlike channels_list which returns all workspace channels, this returns only channels you have joined. Useful on large workspaces where channels_list returns thousands of results.

channel_types.description: Comma-separated channel types. Allowed values: 'mpim', 'im', 'public_channel', 'private_channel'. Default: 'public_channel,private_channel'.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (1-999).

tools.name: conversations_history
tools.description: Get messages from the channel (or DM) by channel_id, the last row/column in the response is used as 'cursor' parameter for pagination if not empty

channel_id.description: - `channel_id` (string): ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... or @... aka #general or @username_dm.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value of the last row and column in the response as next_cursor field returned from the previous request.

include_activity_messages.description: If true, the response will include activity messages such as 'channel_join' or 'channel_leave'. Default is boolean false.

limit.description: Limit of messages to fetch in format of maximum ranges of time (e.g. 1d - 1 day, 1w - 1 week, 30d - 30 days, 90d - 90 days which is a default limit for free tier history) or number of messages (e.g. 50). Must be empty when 'cursor' is provided.

tools.name: conversations_join
tools.description: Join a public channel. Use channels_list or channels_me to find channel IDs.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... (e.g., #general).

tools.name: conversations_leave
tools.description: Leave a channel, group conversation, or DM. Cannot leave the #general channel.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... or @... (e.g., #general, @username).

tools.name: conversations_mark
tools.description: Mark a channel or DM as read. If no timestamp is provided, marks all messages as read.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... or @... (e.g., #general, @username).

ts.description: Timestamp of the message to mark as read up to. If not provided, marks all messages as read.

tools.name: conversations_replies
tools.description: Get a thread of messages posted to a conversation by channelID and thread_ts, the last row/column in the response is used as 'cursor' parameter for pagination if not empty

channel_id.description: ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... or @... aka #general or @username_dm.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value of the last row and column in the response as next_cursor field returned from the previous request.

include_activity_messages.description: If true, the response will include activity messages such as 'channel_join' or 'channel_leave'. Default is boolean false.

limit.description: Limit of messages to fetch in format of maximum ranges of time (e.g. 1d - 1 day, 30d - 30 days, 90d - 90 days which is a default limit for free tier history) or number of messages (e.g. 50). Must be empty when 'cursor' is provided.

thread_ts.description: Unique identifier of either a thread's parent message or a message in the thread. ts must be the timestamp in format 1234567890.123456 of an existing message with 0 or more replies.

tools.name: conversations_search_messages
tools.description: Search messages in a public channel, private channel, or direct message (DM, or IM) conversation using filters. All filters are optional, if not provided then search_query is required.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value of the last row and column in the response as next_cursor field returned from the previous request.

filter_date_after.description: Filter messages sent after a specific date in format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Example: '2023-10-01', 'July', 'Yesterday' or 'Today'. If not provided, all dates will be searched.

filter_date_before.description: Filter messages sent before a specific date in format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Example: '2023-10-01', 'July', 'Yesterday' or 'Today'. If not provided, all dates will be searched.

filter_date_during.description: Filter messages sent during a specific period in format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Example: 'July', 'Yesterday' or 'Today'. If not provided, all dates will be searched.

filter_date_on.description: Filter messages sent on a specific date in format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Example: '2023-10-01', 'July', 'Yesterday' or 'Today'. If not provided, all dates will be searched.

filter_in_channel.description: Filter messages in a specific public/private channel by its ID or name. Example: 'C1234567890', 'G1234567890', or '#general'. If not provided, all channels will be searched.

filter_in_im_or_mpim.description: Filter messages in a direct message (DM) or multi-person direct message (MPIM) conversation by its ID or name. Example: 'D1234567890' or '@username_dm'. If not provided, all DMs and MPIMs will be searched.

filter_threads_only.description: If true, the response will include only messages from threads. Default is boolean false.

filter_users_from.description: Filter messages from a specific user by their ID or display name. Example: 'U1234567890' or '@username'. If not provided, all users will be searched.

filter_users_with.description: Filter messages with a specific user by their ID or display name in threads and DMs. Example: 'U1234567890' or '@username'. If not provided, all threads and DMs will be searched.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Must be an integer between 1 and 100.

search_query.description: Search query to filter messages. Example: 'marketing report' or full URL of Slack message e.g. 'https://slack.com/archives/C1234567890/p1234567890123456', then the tool will return a single message matching given URL, herewith all other parameters will be ignored.

tools.name: conversations_unreads
tools.description: Get unread messages across all channels. With browser session tokens (xoxc/xoxd), uses a single API call for complete results. With OAuth user tokens (xoxp), scans a subset of channels per type (limited by max_channels) Р В Р вЂ Р В РІР‚С™Р Р†Р вЂљРЎСљ results may be partial on large workspaces. Results are prioritized: DMs > group DMs > partner channels > internal channels.

channel_types.description: Filter by channel type: 'all' (default), 'dm' (direct messages), 'group_dm' (group DMs), 'partner' (ext-* channels), 'internal' (other channels).

include_messages.description: If true (default), returns the actual unread messages. If false, returns only a summary of channels with unreads.

include_muted.description: If true, includes muted channels in results. Default is false (muted channels are excluded, matching Slack app behavior).

max_channels.description: Maximum number of channels to fetch unreads from. Default is 50.

max_messages_per_channel.description: Maximum messages to fetch per channel. Default is 10.

mentions_only.description: If true, only returns channels where you have @mentions. Default is false.

tools.name: usergroups_create
tools.description: Create a new user group (mention group) in the Slack workspace. After creation, use usergroups_users_update to add members, or users can join themselves with usergroups_me. The handle becomes the @mention (e.g., handle='engineering' creates @engineering).

channels.description: Comma-separated channel IDs where this group is commonly mentioned. Members get suggestions to join these channels.

description.description: Purpose or description shown in group details (e.g., 'Backend and frontend engineers').

handle.description: The @mention handle without the @ symbol (e.g., 'engineering' for @engineering). Keep it short and lowercase. If omitted, Slack auto-generates one from the name.

name.description: Display name of the user group (e.g., 'Engineering Team', 'Design Squad').

tools.name: usergroups_list
tools.description: List all user groups (subteams) in the Slack workspace. User groups are mention groups like @engineering or @design that notify all members. Use this to discover available groups, check group membership counts, or find a group's ID before joining/updating it. Returns CSV with columns: id, name, handle, description, user_count, is_external.

include_count.description: Include user count for each group. Default is true.

include_disabled.description: Include disabled/archived groups. Default is false.

include_users.description: Include list of user IDs in each group. Default is false.

tools.name: usergroups_me
tools.description: Manage your own user group membership. Use action='list' to see which groups you belong to. Use action='join' with a usergroup_id to add yourself to a group (e.g., to receive @mentions). Use action='leave' with a usergroup_id to remove yourself. This is the easiest way to join/leave groups without needing to know the full member list.

action.description: Action to perform: 'list' returns CSV of groups you're a member of, 'join' adds you to a group, 'leave' removes you from a group.

usergroup_id.description: ID of the user group (starts with 'S', e.g., 'S0123456789'). Required for 'join' and 'leave' actions. Get IDs from usergroups_list.

tools.name: usergroups_update
tools.description: Update a user group's metadata: name, handle (@mention), description, or default channels. Does NOT change members - use usergroups_users_update for that. At least one field must be provided.

channels.description: New default channel IDs (comma-separated). Replaces existing default channels.

handle.description: New @mention handle (without @). Changing this changes how users mention the group.

name.description: New display name for the group.

usergroup_id.description: ID of the user group to update (starts with 'S', e.g., 'S0123456789'). Get IDs from usergroups_list.

tools.name: usergroups_users_update
tools.description: Replace all members of a user group with a new list. WARNING: This completely replaces the member list - any user not in the 'users' parameter will be removed. To add/remove just yourself, use usergroups_me instead. To add a single user without removing others, first get current members from usergroups_list with include_users=true, then call this with the combined list.

usergroup_id.description: ID of the user group (starts with 'S', e.g., 'S0123456789'). Get IDs from usergroups_list.

users.description: Comma-separated user IDs that will become the COMPLETE member list (e.g., 'U0123456789,U9876543210'). All current members not in this list will be removed.

tools.name: users_search
tools.description: Search for users by name, email, display name, or Slack user ID. If a Slack user ID is provided (e.g. U07VCEPP4N5), the user is looked up directly. Returns user details and DM channel ID if available.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100). Default is 10.

query.description: Search query - matches against real name, display name, username, email, or a Slack user ID (e.g. U07VCEPP4N5).

tools.name: get_gmail_message_content
tools.description:
Retrieves the full content (subject, sender, recipients, body) of a specific Gmail message.

Bodies are returned inline and truncated at 20,000 characters. Set full=True to
get the complete, untruncated message instead: it is exported to storage and the
response carries a short-lived download URL (HTTP transport) or file path (stdio
transport) rather than the body, so large messages never stream through the model
context. Stateless deployments without GCS staging have no storage, so there
full=True returns the untruncated body inline; with GCS staging configured it
returns a signed download URL like any other HTTP deployment.

message_id.description: The unique ID of the Gmail message to retrieve.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

body_format.description: Body output format (only applies when format='full'). 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches the full raw MIME message and returns the base64url-decoded content.

full.description: When True, return the COMPLETE untruncated message: saved to storage and referenced by download URL/file path instead of the body text. In stateless mode without GCS staging, the body is returned inline; with GCS staging, a signed download URL is returned. Use for messages large enough to hit the truncation limit, or when byte-exact fidelity is needed (pair with body_format='raw' for a .eml export).

format.description:
Message format. "full" (default) includes
the body and attachments, "metadata" only headers.

tools.description:

Supports up to 25 messages per batch to prevent SSL connection exhaustion.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

format.description: Message format. "full" includes body, "metadata" only headers.

body_format.description: Body output format (only applies when format='full'). 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches the full raw MIME message and returns the base64url-decoded content.

tools.name: get_gmail_attachment_content
tools.description:
Downloads an email attachment and saves it to local disk.

In stdio mode, returns the local file path for direct access.
In HTTP mode, returns a temporary download URL (valid for 1 hour).
May re-fetch message metadata to resolve filename and MIME type.

message_id.description: The ID of the Gmail message containing the attachment.

attachment_id.description: The ID of the attachment to download.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

return_base64.description:
When True, includes the full attachment as a
standard base64 string in the response (in addition to any file
path or download URL). Useful for sandboxed clients that cannot
reach localhost download URLs or the MCP server's local file
paths (e.g. containerized agents with network allowlists). The
returned base64 uses the standard alphabet, so it can be passed
directly to tools like ``draft_gmail_message`` that expect
standard (not URL-safe) base64. Default False preserves the
existing behavior and response size.

attachment_index.description:
Zero-based attachment position from
the message-content response. Lets the server resolve Gmail's
refreshed attachment IDs against current metadata before every
download, selecting the current attachment ID, filename and MIME type.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required for authentication.

to.description: Recipient email address. Optional when replying with reply_all=True, which derives it from the thread.

subject.description: Email subject. Required when sending; optional when forwarding (defaults to 'Fwd: <original subject>').

body.description: Email body content (plain text or HTML). Required when sending. When forwarding, this is an optional note prepended above the quoted original.

body_format.description: Format of the body content (and of the prepended note when forwarding). Use 'plain' for plaintext or 'html' for HTML content.

forward_message_id.description: Set to a Gmail message ID to forward that message instead of composing a new one. The original subject, body, and (optionally) attachments are carried over; 'body' becomes an optional note prepended to the forward.

include_forwarded_attachments.description: When forwarding, whether to include the original message's attachments. Ignored unless forward_message_id is set.

from_name.description: Optional sender display name (e.g., 'Peter Hartree'). If provided, the From header will be formatted as 'Name <email>'.

from_email.description: Optional 'Send As' alias email address. Must be configured in Gmail settings (Settings > Accounts > Send mail as). If not provided, uses the authenticated user's email.

thread_id.description: Optional Gmail thread ID to reply within. When in_reply_to is omitted, replies to the latest non-draft, non-trash message with an RFC Message-ID.

in_reply_to.description: Optional RFC Message-ID to explicitly reply to a specific message (e.g., '<message123@gmail.com>'). Omit to reply to the latest eligible message in thread_id.

references.description: Optional Message-ID ancestry chain. Normally omit when thread_id is provided; the server derives the chain through the selected reply target.

attachments.description: Optional list of attachments. Each can have: "url" (fetch from URL — works with MCP attachment URLs from get_drive_file_download_url / get_gmail_attachment_content), OR "path" (file path, auto-encodes), OR "content" (standard base64, not urlsafe) + "filename". Optional "mime_type". Optional "content_id" (string) makes the attachment inline-rendered: it lands in a multipart/related part with `Content-ID: ` and `Content-Disposition: inline`, and the HTML body can reference it via `` (RFC 2392). Without `content_id` the attachment is a regular multipart/mixed attachment. Example: [{"url": "https://host/attachments/abc-123", "filename": "report.pdf"}]

include_signature.description: Whether to append the Gmail signature from Settings > Signature when available. Defaults to true.

quote_original.description: Whether to include the message being replied to as a quoted original. Only has an effect when thread_id is provided. Defaults to false.

reply_all.description: Whether to derive reply-all recipients from the thread: To = the sender being replied to, Cc = the other participants, excluding the authenticated account and from_email. Requires thread_id. Explicit to/cc win; when cc is omitted the sender being replied to is added to the derived Cc if they are not already in To. Defaults to false.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required for authentication.

subject.description: Email subject. Required unless forwarding (then defaults to 'Fwd: <original subject>').

body.description: Email body. Required unless forwarding, where it becomes an optional note prepended above the quoted original.

body_format.description: Email body format. Use 'plain' for plaintext or 'html' for HTML content.

forward_message_id.description: Set to a Gmail message ID to save a forward of that message as a draft for review. The original subject, body, and (optionally) attachments are carried over; 'body' becomes an optional note prepended to the forward.

include_forwarded_attachments.description: When forwarding, whether to include the original message's attachments. Ignored unless forward_message_id is set.

from_name.description: Optional sender display name (e.g., 'Peter Hartree'). If provided, the From header will be formatted as 'Name <email>'.

from_email.description: Optional 'Send As' alias email address. Must be configured in Gmail settings (Settings > Accounts > Send mail as). If not provided, uses the account's default Send As address, falling back to the authenticated user's email when Gmail returns no usable Send-As entry or settings access is not authorized.

thread_id.description: Optional Gmail thread ID to reply within. When in_reply_to is omitted, replies to the latest non-draft, non-trash message with an RFC Message-ID.

in_reply_to.description: Optional RFC Message-ID to explicitly reply to a specific message (e.g., '<message123@gmail.com>'). Omit to reply to the latest eligible message in thread_id.

references.description: Optional Message-ID ancestry chain. Normally omit when thread_id is provided; the server derives the chain through the selected reply target.

attachments.description: Optional list of attachments. Each can have: 'url' (fetch from URL — works with MCP attachment URLs from get_drive_file_download_url / get_gmail_attachment_content), OR 'path' (file path, auto-encodes), OR 'content' (standard base64, not urlsafe) + 'filename'. Optional 'mime_type'. Optional 'content_id' (string) makes the attachment inline-rendered: it lands in a multipart/related part with `Content-ID: ` and `Content-Disposition: inline`, and the HTML body can reference it via `` (RFC 2392). Without `content_id` the attachment is a regular multipart/mixed attachment.

include_signature.description: Whether to append the Gmail signature from Settings > Signature when available. Defaults to true.

quote_original.description: Whether to include the original message as a quoted reply. Only has an effect when thread_id is provided. Defaults to false.

tools.name: get_gmail_thread_content
tools.description:
Retrieves the complete content of a Gmail conversation thread, including all messages.

Optionally also returns structured ownership analysis so a caller can
determine who sent the last message and who owes whom a response without
re-parsing the formatted string or making a second tool call.

thread_id.description: The unique ID of the Gmail thread to retrieve.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

body_format.description: Body output format. 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches each message's full raw MIME content and returns the base64url-decoded body.

include_analysis.description: When True, the return value is a dict with both the formatted thread content AND structured ownership analysis (last sender, ball-in-court verdict, per-sender message counts, participants). Defaults to False, in which case the existing string return shape is preserved.

tools.name: get_gmail_threads_content_batch
tools.description:
Retrieves the content of multiple Gmail threads in a single batch request.
Supports up to 25 threads per batch to prevent SSL connection exhaustion.

thread_ids.description: A list of Gmail thread IDs to retrieve. The function will automatically batch requests in chunks of 25.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

body_format.description: Body output format. 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches each message's full raw MIME content and returns the base64url-decoded body.

tools.name: list_gmail_labels
tools.description: Lists labels in the user's Gmail account.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

prefix.description:
Return only labels whose name starts with this
exact (case-sensitive) string. users.labels.list accepts no filter,
so the full list is fetched and narrowed here: this shrinks what the
caller receives, not the API call.

include_system.description:
Include Gmail system labels (INBOX, SENT, ...).
Set False to return user labels only.

tools.name: manage_gmail_label
tools.description: Manages Gmail labels: create, update, or delete labels.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

action.description: Action to perform on the label.

name.description: Label name. Required for create, optional for update.

label_id.description: Label ID. Required for update and delete operations.

label_list_visibility.description: Whether the label is shown in the label list. Defaults to "labelShow" on create. On update, omitting it keeps the label's current setting.

message_list_visibility.description: Whether the label's messages are shown in the message list. Defaults to "show" on create. On update, omitting it keeps the label's current setting.

background_color.description: Label background color as a hex string, e.g. "#fb4c2f". Set together with text_color; Gmail requires both. Gmail accepts only its own palette, and an unsupported value is rejected before the request. Colors apply to user labels, not system labels.

text_color.description: Label text color as a hex string, e.g. "#ffffff". Set together with background_color. Same palette. On update, omitting both keeps the label's current color.

clear_color.description: On update, remove the label's current color. Cannot be combined with background_color or text_color.

tools.name: list_gmail_filters
tools.description: Lists all Gmail filters configured in the user's mailbox.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

tools.name: manage_gmail_filter
tools.description:
Manages Gmail filters: create, delete, update, and apply to existing mail.

- update: Gmail has no filter update API, so the filter is recreated (new
  one first, then the old one is deleted) and its ID changes. A passed
  criteria or filter_action replaces that whole object; omit one to keep
  the old filter's.
- apply: runs a filter's label actions on mail ALREADY in the mailbox
  (Gmail filters only act on new mail). Only matching messages change,
  not whole conversations as in the web UI. Use filter_id, or criteria +
  filter_action for an ad-hoc run. Forwarding is never applied. Use
  dry_run=true first to see the search query and the match count.
  Needs the gmail.modify scope in addition to gmail.settings.basic.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

action.description: "create", "delete", "update" or "apply".

criteria.description: Filter criteria object (required for create; optional for update/apply).

filter_action.description: Filter action object (required for create; optional for update/apply). Named 'filter_action' to avoid shadowing the 'action' parameter.

filter_id.description: ID of the filter (required for delete and update; optional for apply).

dry_run.description: apply only: count matches without changing anything.

max_messages.description: apply only: safety cap on messages changed (default 5000).

tools.name: modify_gmail_message_labels
tools.description:
Adds or removes labels from a Gmail message.
To archive an email, remove the INBOX label.
To delete an email, add the TRASH label.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

message_id.description: The ID of the message to modify.

add_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to add to the message.

remove_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to remove from the message.

tools.name: batch_modify_gmail_message_labels
tools.description:
Adds or removes labels from multiple Gmail messages in a single batch request.

Takes MESSAGE ids, not thread ids. Gmail's batch endpoint returns no
per-message result and silently ignores ids it does not recognise, so by
default this reads the messages back afterwards and reports which ids
actually changed.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

message_ids.description: A list of message IDs to modify.

add_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to add to the messages.

remove_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to remove from the messages.

verify.description:
Read the messages back and report per-id outcomes. Costs
one extra (batched) read per id. Set False for very large sweeps
where that cost matters and an unverified result is acceptable.

tools.name: search_drive_files
tools.description: Searches for files and folders within a user's Google Drive, including shared drives.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

query.description:
The search query string. Supports Google Drive search operators.
         NOTE: Owner-based queries ('user@example.com' in owners) DO NOT WORK in Shared Drives
         because files are owned by the shared drive itself, not individual users.
         For recent files by a specific user in Shared Drives, search by modifiedTime
         and use order_by='modifiedTime desc' instead.

page_size.description: The maximum number of files to return. Defaults to 10.

page_token.description: Page token from a previous response's nextPageToken to retrieve the next page of results.

drive_id.description: ID of the shared drive to search. If None, behavior depends on `corpora` and `include_items_from_all_drives`.

include_items_from_all_drives.description: Whether shared drive items should be included in results. Defaults to True. This is effective when not specifying a `drive_id`.

corpora.description:
Bodies of items to query (e.g., 'user', 'domain', 'drive', 'allDrives').
                     If 'drive_id' is specified and 'corpora' is None, it defaults to 'drive'.
                     Otherwise it defaults to 'allDrives' when `include_items_from_all_drives` is True.
                     Pass 'user' to search only My Drive and files shared with the user.

file_type.description:
Restrict results to a specific file type. Accepts a friendly
                       name ('folder', 'document'/'doc', 'spreadsheet'/'sheet',
                       'presentation'/'slides', 'form', 'drawing', 'pdf', 'shortcut',
                       'script', 'site', 'jam'/'jamboard') or any raw MIME type
                       string (e.g. 'application/pdf'). Defaults to None (all types).

detailed.description: Whether to include size, modified time, and link in results. Defaults to True.

order_by.description:
Sort order. Comma-separated list of sort keys with optional 'desc' modifier.
                      Valid keys: 'createdTime', 'folder', 'modifiedByMeTime', 'modifiedTime',
                      'name', 'name_natural', 'quotaBytesUsed', 'recency', 'sharedWithMeTime',
                      'starred', 'viewedByMeTime'. Example: 'modifiedTime desc' or 'folder,modifiedTime desc,name'.
                      Defaults to None (Drive API default ordering).

include_trashed.description:
Whether to include files in the trash. Defaults to False, matching
                    the Drive web UI and `list_drive_items`. Ignored when `query` already
                    contains its own `trashed` clause (`=` or `!=`), which always wins.

tools.name: get_drive_file_content
tools.description:
Retrieves the content of a specific Google Drive file by ID, supporting files in shared drives.

• Native Google Docs, Sheets, Slides → exported as text / CSV.
• Office files (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx) → unzipped & parsed with std-lib to
  extract readable text.
• PDFs → text extracted with pypdf when possible; scanned/image-only PDFs
  fall back to a download hint.
• Images → returned as base64 with MIME metadata for multimodal clients.
• Any other file → downloaded; tries UTF-8 decode, else notes binary.

user_google_email.description: The user’s Google email address.

tools.name: get_drive_file_download_url
tools.description:
Downloads a Google Drive file and saves it to local disk.

In stdio mode, returns the local file path for direct access.
In HTTP mode, returns a temporary download URL (valid for 1 hour).
In stateless mode (no file storage), returns the file itself as an embedded
resource, up to WORKSPACE_MCP_STATELESS_INLINE_MAX_BYTES (default 10 MiB,
and never more than WORKSPACE_MCP_MAX_FILE_BYTES when that is set).

For Google native files (Docs, Sheets, Slides), exports to a useful format:
- Google Docs -> PDF (default) or DOCX if export_format='docx'
- Google Sheets -> XLSX (default), PDF if export_format='pdf', or CSV if export_format='csv'
- Google Slides -> PDF (default) or PPTX if export_format='pptx'

For other files, downloads the original file format.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_id.description: The Google Drive file ID to download.

export_format.description:
Optional export format for Google native files.
          Options: 'pdf', 'docx', 'xlsx', 'csv', 'pptx'.
          If not specified, uses sensible defaults (PDF for Docs/Slides, XLSX for Sheets).
          For Sheets: supports 'csv', 'pdf', or 'xlsx' (default).

tools.name: list_drive_items
tools.description:
Lists files/folders or shared drive containers, supporting shared drives.
If `drive_id` is specified, lists items within that shared drive. `folder_id` is then relative to that drive (or use drive_id as folder_id for root).
If `drive_id` is not specified, lists items from user's "My Drive" and accessible shared drives (if `include_items_from_all_drives` is True).
Set `resource_type` to "shared_drives" to list shared drive containers instead of folder contents.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

folder_id.description: The ID of the Google Drive folder. Defaults to 'root'. For a shared drive, this can be the shared drive's ID to list its root, or a folder ID within that shared drive.

page_size.description: The maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 100.

page_token.description: Page token from a previous response's nextPageToken to retrieve the next page of results.

drive_id.description: ID of the shared drive. If provided, the listing is scoped to this drive.

include_items_from_all_drives.description: Whether items from all accessible shared drives should be included if `drive_id` is not set. Defaults to True.

corpora.description: Corpus to query ('user', 'drive', 'allDrives'). If `drive_id` is set and `corpora` is None, 'drive' is used. If None and no `drive_id`, 'allDrives' is used when `include_items_from_all_drives` is True.

file_type.description:
Restrict results to a specific file type. Accepts a friendly
                       name ('folder', 'document'/'doc', 'spreadsheet'/'sheet',
                       'presentation'/'slides', 'form', 'drawing', 'pdf', 'shortcut',
                       'script', 'site', 'jam'/'jamboard') or any raw MIME type
                       string (e.g. 'application/pdf'). Defaults to None (all types).

detailed.description: Whether to include size, modified time, and link in results. Defaults to True.

order_by.description:
Sort order. Comma-separated list of sort keys with optional 'desc' modifier.
                      Valid keys: 'createdTime', 'folder', 'modifiedByMeTime', 'modifiedTime',
                      'name', 'name_natural', 'quotaBytesUsed', 'recency', 'sharedWithMeTime',
                      'starred', 'viewedByMeTime'. Example: 'modifiedTime desc' or 'folder,modifiedTime desc,name'.
                      Defaults to None (Drive API default ordering).

resource_type.description:
What to list. Use "items" for folder contents or
                 "shared_drives" for shared drive containers. Defaults to "items".

query.description:
Shared drive query used only when resource_type="shared_drives",
                   e.g. "name contains 'Engineering'".

include_organizers.description:
When resource_type="shared_drives", include principals
                       with the organizer role. This costs one extra permissions.list
                       API call per shared drive returned. Defaults to False.

tools.name: create_drive_folder
tools.description: Creates a new folder in Google Drive, supporting creation within shared drives.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

folder_name.description: The name for the new folder.

parent_folder_id.description:
The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'.
For shared drives, use a folder ID within that shared drive.

tools.name: create_drive_file
tools.description:
Creates a new file in Google Drive, supporting creation within shared drives.
Accepts direct text content, inline base64 bytes, or a fileUrl to fetch content from.
This stores the supplied bytes without converting them to Google Docs, Sheets, or
Slides. Use the matching import_to_google_* tool for Google-native conversion.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_name.description: The name for the new file.

content.description: If provided, the content to write to the file.

folder_id.description: The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'. For shared drives, this must be a folder ID within the shared drive.

mime_type.description: The MIME type of the file. Defaults to 'text/plain'; required with return_upload_url.

fileUrl.description: If provided, fetches the file content from this URL. Supports file://, http://, and https:// protocols.

base64_sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 of decoded base64_content. Recommended for binary payload integrity checks.

tools.name: import_to_google_doc
tools.description:
Imports a file (Markdown, DOCX, TXT, HTML, RTF, ODT) into Google Docs format with automatic conversion.

Google Drive automatically converts the source file to native Google Docs format,
preserving formatting like headings, lists, bold, italic, etc.
Binary sources may be passed directly as base64_content. On a local server a
file on disk can also be passed by path (preferred for batch operations, so
callers do not need to load full file contents into their context).

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_name.description: The name for the new Google Doc (extension will be ignored).

content.description: Text content for text-based formats. Use only for short snippets or content already in memory.

file_path.description: Local file path or file:// URL for any supported format (MD, TXT, HTML, DOCX, ODT, RTF). Appropriate for larger files than content, but file_path may still load the file into memory or perform non-streaming reads. Avoid very large files that could exceed memory or time limits; use streaming/chunked uploads or an alternative API for huge files.

file_url.description: Remote URL to fetch the file from (http/https).

source_format.description:
Source format hint ('md', 'markdown', 'docx', 'txt', 'html', 'rtf', 'odt').
                           Auto-detected from file_name extension if not provided.

folder_id.description: The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'.

base64_content.description: Standard base64-encoded bytes for a binary source such as DOCX or ODT.

base64_sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 of decoded base64_content. Recommended for binary payload integrity checks.

tools.name: import_to_google_slides
tools.description:
Imports a presentation (PPTX, PPT, ODP) into Google Slides format with automatic conversion.

Google Drive automatically converts the source presentation to native Google Slides format,
preserving slides, layouts, text, and images.
Binary sources may be passed directly as base64_content. On a local server a
file on disk can also be passed by path (preferred for batch operations, so
callers do not need to load full file contents into their context).

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_name.description: The name for the new Google Slides presentation (extension will be ignored).

file_path.description: Local file path or file:// URL for any supported format (PPTX, PPT, ODP). Appropriate for larger files than content, but file_path may still load the file into memory or perform non-streaming reads. Avoid very large files that could exceed memory or time limits; use streaming/chunked uploads or an alternative API for huge files.

file_url.description: Remote URL to fetch the presentation from (http/https).

source_format.description:
Source format hint ('pptx', 'ppt', 'odp').
                           Auto-detected from file_name extension if not provided.

folder_id.description: The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'.

base64_content.description: Standard base64-encoded bytes for a PPTX or ODP source.

base64_sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 of decoded base64_content. Recommended for binary payload integrity checks.

tools.name: import_to_google_sheets
tools.description:
Imports a spreadsheet (XLSX, XLS, ODS, CSV, TSV) into Google Sheets format with automatic conversion.

Google Drive automatically converts the source spreadsheet to native Google Sheets format,
preserving rows, columns, sheets, and values.
Binary sources may be passed directly as base64_content. On a local server a
file on disk can also be passed by path (preferred for batch operations, so
callers do not need to load full file contents into their context).

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_name.description: The name for the new Google Sheets spreadsheet (extension will be ignored).

content.description: Text content for text-based formats (CSV, TSV). Use only for short snippets or content already in memory.

file_path.description: Local file path or file:// URL for any supported format (XLSX, XLS, ODS, CSV, TSV). Appropriate for larger files than content, but file_path may still load the file into memory or perform non-streaming reads. Avoid very large files that could exceed memory or time limits; use streaming/chunked uploads or an alternative API for huge files.

file_url.description: Remote URL to fetch the spreadsheet from (http/https).

source_format.description:
Source format hint ('xlsx', 'xls', 'ods', 'csv', 'tsv').
                           Auto-detected from file_name extension if not provided.

folder_id.description: The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'.

base64_content.description: Standard base64-encoded bytes for an XLSX, XLS, or ODS source.

base64_sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 of decoded base64_content. Recommended for binary payload integrity checks.

tools.name: get_drive_file_permissions
tools.description:
Gets detailed metadata about a Google Drive file including sharing permissions,
parent folder IDs, ownership, and lifecycle timestamps.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_id.description: The ID of the file to check permissions for.

tools.name: check_drive_file_public_access
tools.description: Searches for a file by name and checks if it has public link sharing enabled.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_name.description: The name of the file to check.

drive_id.description:
ID of the shared drive to scope the search to. When set, the
                      underlying files.list call uses corpora='drive' and the given
                      driveId, which is required to reliably find files that live only
                      in that shared drive. When None, behaviour is unchanged
                      (default API corpora applies).

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_id.description: The ID of the file to update. Required.

mime_type.description:
New MIME type (note: changing type may require
content upload). For a shortcut ID, this must accompany content and applies
to the resolved target.

add_parents.description: Comma-separated folder IDs to add as parents.

remove_parents.description: Comma-separated folder IDs to remove from parents.

trashed.description: Whether to move file to/from trash.

writers_can_share.description:
Whether editors can share the file. Pass the
target ID directly; this cannot be changed on a shortcut resource.

copy_requires_writer_permission.description:
Whether copying requires writer
permission. Pass the target ID directly; this cannot be changed on a
shortcut resource.

properties.description: Custom key-value properties for the file.

content.description: New text content for text-based formats (markdown, TXT, HTML).

file_path.description: Local file path for binary formats (DOCX, ODT). Supports file:// URLs.

file_url.description: Remote http(s) URL to fetch new content from.

source_format.description:
Source format hint for conversion
(md, markdown, docx, txt, html, rtf, odt). Auto-detected when omitted, and
ignored for non-Google files, which are uploaded without conversion.
Provide at most one content source.

mode.description:
How to apply the new content — 'replace' (default), 'append', or
'prepend'. Append/prepend require 'content' and a UTF-8 text file such as
.md or .txt; a newline is inserted at the seam if neither side has one.
For native Google Docs use insert_doc_elements, modify_doc_text, or
find_and_replace_doc, which edit in place instead of rewriting the file.

tools.name: get_drive_shareable_link
tools.description: Gets the shareable link for a Google Drive file or folder.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_id.description: The ID of the file or folder to get the shareable link for. Required.

tools.name: manage_drive_access
tools.description:
Consolidated tool for managing Google Drive file and folder access permissions.

Supports granting, batch-granting, updating, revoking permissions, and
transferring file ownership -- all through a single entry point.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_id.description: The ID of the file or folder. Required.

action.description:
The access management action to perform. Required. One of:
- "grant": Share with a single user, group, domain, or anyone.
- "grant_batch": Share with multiple recipients in one call.
- "update": Modify an existing permission (role or expiration).
- "revoke": Remove an existing permission.
- "transfer_owner": Transfer file ownership to another user.

share_with.description:
Email address (user/group), domain name (domain),
or omit for 'anyone'. Used by "grant".

role.description:
Permission role -- 'reader', 'commenter', or 'writer'.
Used by "grant" (defaults to 'reader') and "update".

share_type.description:
Type of sharing -- 'user', 'group', 'domain', or 'anyone'.
Used by "grant". Defaults to 'user'.

permission_id.description:
The permission ID to modify or remove.
Required for "update" and "revoke" actions.

recipients.description:
List of recipient objects for
"grant_batch". Each should have: email (str), role (str, optional),
share_type (str, optional), expiration_time (str, optional). For domain
shares use 'domain' field instead of 'email'.

send_notification.description:
Whether to send notification emails. Defaults to True.
Used by "grant" and "grant_batch".

email_message.description:
Custom notification email message.
Used by "grant" and "grant_batch".

expiration_time.description:
Expiration in RFC 3339 format
(e.g., "2025-01-15T00:00:00Z"). Used by "grant" and "update".

allow_file_discovery.description:
For 'domain'/'anyone' shares, whether
the file appears in search. Used by "grant".

new_owner_email.description:
Email of the new owner.
Required for "transfer_owner".

move_to_new_owners_root.description:
Move file to the new owner's My Drive root.
Defaults to False. Used by "transfer_owner".

tools.name: copy_drive_file
tools.description:
Creates a copy of an existing Google Drive file.

This tool copies the template document to a new location with an optional new name.
The copy maintains all formatting and content from the original file.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_id.description: The ID of the file to copy. Required.

new_name.description: New name for the copied file. If not provided, uses "Copy of [original name]".

parent_folder_id.description: The ID of the folder where the copy should be created. Defaults to 'root' (My Drive).

tools.name: set_drive_file_permissions
tools.description:
Sets file-level sharing settings and controls link sharing for a Google Drive file or folder.

This is a high-level tool for the most common permission changes. Use this to toggle
"anyone with the link" access or configure file-level sharing behavior. For managing
individual user/group permissions, use share_drive_file or update_drive_permission instead.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_id.description: The ID of the file or folder. Required.

link_sharing.description:

- "off": Disable "anyone with the link" access for this file.
- "reader": Anyone with the link can view.
- "commenter": Anyone with the link can comment.
- "writer": Anyone with the link can edit.

writers_can_share.description:
Whether editors can change permissions and share.
If False, only the owner can share. Defaults to None (no change).

Whether viewers and commenters
are prevented from copying, printing, or downloading. Defaults to None (no change).
