tools.name: get_events
tools.description:
Retrieves events from a specified Google Calendar. Can retrieve a single event by ID or multiple events within a time range.
You can also search for events by keyword by supplying the optional "query" param.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

calendar_id.description: The ID of the calendar to query. Use 'primary' for the user's primary calendar. Defaults to 'primary'. Calendar IDs can be obtained using `list_calendars`.

event_id.description: The ID of a specific event to retrieve. If provided, retrieves only this event and ignores time filtering parameters.

time_min.description: The start of the time range (inclusive) in RFC3339 format (e.g., '2024-05-12T10:00:00Z' or '2024-05-12'). If omitted, defaults to the current time when single_events=True. It is omitted from unexpanded queries so recurring masters that began in the past but still have future occurrences remain discoverable. Ignored if event_id is provided.

time_max.description: The end of the time range (exclusive) in RFC3339 format. If omitted, events starting from `time_min` onwards are considered (up to `max_results`). Ignored if event_id is provided.

max_results.description: The maximum number of events to return in one page. Defaults to 25. Ignored if event_id is provided.

query.description: A keyword to search for within event fields (summary, description, location). Ignored if event_id is provided.

detailed.description: Whether to return detailed event information including description, location, colour (colorId), attendees, and attendee details (response status, organizer, optional flags). Recurring instances also report the parent series ID needed to edit the whole series; recurring masters report their raw RFC5545 recurrence rules; and events that are not ordinary confirmed meetings report their event type (outOfOffice, workingLocation, focusTime) and status. Defaults to False.

include_attachments.description: Whether to include attachment information in detailed event output. When True, shows attachment details (fileId, fileUrl, mimeType, title) for events that have attachments. Only applies when detailed=True. Set this to True when you need to view or access files that have been attached to calendar events, such as meeting documents, presentations, or other shared files. Defaults to False.

single_events.description: Whether to expand recurring series into individual instances. Defaults to True for backwards compatibility. Set to False with detailed=True to retrieve recurring master events and their exact RFC5545 recurrence rules instead of inferring cadence from expanded instances.

page_token.description: Token for the next page, taken from a previous response. When single_events=True, also pass the response's Pagination time_min as time_min, even if omitted on the first call. Keep all other query parameters unchanged. Ignored if event_id is provided.

tools.name: manage_event
tools.description: Manages calendar events. Supports creating, updating, deleting, and RSVP.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

action.description: Action to perform - "create", "update", "delete", or "rsvp".

start_time.description: Start time (required for create). An RFC3339 UTC offset identifies the exact instant and is preserved. Without an offset, supply start_timezone or timezone. For a local wall-clock time, omit the offset and pass the zone so Google resolves daylight saving; a wrong offset moves the event. Date-only values create all-day events.

end_time.description: End time (required for create). An RFC3339 UTC offset identifies the exact instant and is preserved. Without an offset, supply end_timezone or timezone. All-day end dates are exclusive.

event_id.description: Event ID (required for update and delete).

attendees.description: Attendee email addresses, attendee objects (e.g. {"email": ..., "responseStatus": "accepted"}), or a mix of both.

timezone.description:
IANA timezone applied to both boundaries (e.g.,
"America/New_York"). Converts offset-bearing timestamps without changing their
instant; interprets offset-free timestamps as local times in this zone.
Overridden per boundary by start_timezone/end_timezone.

attachments.description:
List of Google Drive file URLs or IDs to attach.
On action="update" this replaces the event's existing attachments rather than
appending to them, matching the Calendar API's patch semantics.

add_google_meet.description: Whether to add/remove native Google Meet.

conference_data.description:
Raw Google Calendar `conferenceData`
payload to attach a third-party conference (Zoom/Webex/Teams add-on). Use this
for full control; mutually exclusive with the conference_provider helper params
and with add_google_meet. (create/update only)

conference_provider.description:
Higher-level helper: third-party provider name
(e.g. "zoom", "webex", "teams"). Requires conference_uri. The MCP builds the
addOn `conferenceData` block internally. (create/update only)

conference_uri.description:
Join URL for the third-party conference (e.g.
"https://zoom.us/j/123456789"). Required when conference_provider is set.

conference_passcode.description: Optional passcode for the third-party conference.

transparency.description: "opaque" (busy) or "transparent" (free).

recurrence.description: RFC5545 recurrence rules for a recurring event, e.g. ["RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=10"].

guests_can_see_other_guests.description: Whether attendees can see other guests.

rsvp_comment.description: Optional message to include with the RSVP response (rsvp action only).

send_updates.description: Notification behavior for create, update, delete, and rsvp — "all" (default), "externalOnly", or "none".

start_timezone.description:
IANA timezone for the start boundary only,
overriding timezone. Use for events whose two ends sit in different zones -
a flight departing 13:45 "Asia/Jerusalem" and landing 17:50
"Europe/Amsterdam" is one event authored in two zones. Explicit timestamp
offsets always preserve the instant, even when the zone differs.

end_timezone.description:
IANA timezone for the end boundary only,
overriding timezone. See start_timezone.

tools.name: manage_out_of_office
tools.description:
Manages Out of Office events on Google Calendar. These special events auto-decline
meeting invitations and set the user's status to "Out of office" across Google Workspace.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

action.description: Action to perform - "create", "list", "update", or "delete".

start_time.description: Start date/time. Use 'YYYY-MM-DD' for full-day or RFC3339 for partial-day (e.g., '2024-04-05T09:00:00Z'). Date-only values are auto-converted to dateTime (midnight-to-midnight). Required for create.

end_time.description: End date/time (exclusive). Same format as start_time. For a single full day on April 5, use start_time='2026-04-05' and end_time='2026-04-06'. Required for create.

summary.description: Display text on the calendar. Defaults to "Out of Office".

auto_decline_mode.description: How to handle conflicting invitations. One of: "declineAllConflictingInvitations" (default), "declineOnlyNewConflictingInvitations", "declineNone".

recurrence.description: RFC5545 recurrence rules for a recurring Out of Office series, e.g. ["RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=10"].

timezone.description: Timezone for the event (e.g., "America/New_York", "Europe/London"). Required when using date-only values or dateTime values without an explicit UTC offset.

time_min.description: For "list" action: start of time range. Defaults to current time. Recurring series are expanded into individual instances in the requested range.

time_max.description: For "list" action: end of time range.

max_results.description: For "list" action: maximum events to return in one page. Defaults to 10.

event_id.description: Event ID. Required for "update" and "delete" actions.

calendar_id.description: Calendar ID. Defaults to 'primary'. Out of Office status events live on primary calendars, so use 'primary' or a user's primary calendar ID/email rather than a secondary calendar ID.

page_token.description: For "list" action: token for the next page, taken from a previous response. Also pass the response's Pagination time_min as time_min, even if omitted on the first call. Keep all other query parameters unchanged.

tools.name: manage_focus_time
tools.description:
Manages Focus Time events on Google Calendar. These special events auto-decline
meeting invitations and, by default, set the user's chat status to Do Not
Disturb, helping protect blocks of uninterrupted work time.

action.description: Action to perform - "create", "list", "update", or "delete".

end_time.description: End date/time (exclusive). Same format as start_time. For a single full day on April 5, use start_time='2026-04-05' and end_time='2026-04-06'. Required for create.

summary.description: Display text on the calendar. Defaults to "Focus Time".

description.description: Event description. Useful for adding context about what the focus time is for.

auto_decline_mode.description: How to handle conflicting invitations. One of: "declineAllConflictingInvitations" (default), "declineOnlyNewConflictingInvitations", "declineNone".

chat_status.description: Google Chat status during the focus time. Supports "doNotDisturb" (default) and "available".

recurrence.description: RFC5545 recurrence rules for a recurring Focus Time series, e.g. ["RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=10"].

timezone.description: Timezone for the event (e.g., "America/New_York", "Europe/London"). Required when using date-only values or dateTime values without an explicit UTC offset.

time_min.description: For "list" action: start of time range. Defaults to current time. Recurring series are expanded into individual instances in the requested range.

time_max.description: For "list" action: end of time range.

max_results.description: For "list" action: maximum events to return in one page. Defaults to 10.

event_id.description: Event ID. Required for "update" and "delete" actions.

calendar_id.description: Calendar ID. Defaults to 'primary'. Focus Time status events live on primary calendars, so use 'primary' or a user's primary calendar ID/email rather than a secondary calendar ID.

Creates a new Google Doc and optionally inserts initial content.

After creation, the document body starts at index 1. A new empty doc
has total length 2 (one section break at index 0, one newline at index 1).

To build a rich document after creation, use batch_update_doc with
insert_text operations using end_of_segment=true to append content
sequentially without calculating indices. Then call inspect_doc_structure
to get exact positions before applying formatting in a separate batch call.

TIP: To append text to the end of the document without calculating indices,

For ordinary header/footer text, prefer update_doc_headers_footers.
Only pass segment_id when you already have a real header/footer/footnote

Finds and replaces text throughout a Google Doc. No index calculation required.

This is the safest way to update specific text in a document because it

- Replace placeholder text (e.g., {{TITLE}}) with real content
- Update specific words or phrases throughout the document
- Make targeted text changes without risk of index errors

          'right', or 'between'); omit to update all four outer edges

border_dash.description: Border dash style ('SOLID', 'DOT', or 'DASH'; defaults to 'SOLID')

list_type.description: Create a list from existing paragraphs ('UNORDERED' for bullets, 'ORDERED' for numbers, 'CHECKBOX' for checklists), or 'NONE' to remove existing list formatting from the range. Use 'NONE' when text inserted after a list has inherited its bullets: setting named_style_type or heading_level does not clear list membership, only 'NONE' does.

list_nesting_level.description:
Nesting level for lists (0-8, where 0 is top level, default is 0)
               Use higher levels for nested/indented list items

bullet_preset.description: Optional explicit Google Docs bullet preset

tools.name: get_doc_as_markdown
tools.description:
Reads a Google Doc and returns it as clean Markdown with optional comment context.

Unlike get_doc_content which returns plain text, this tool preserves document
formatting as Markdown: headings, bold/italic/strikethrough, links, code spans,
ordered/unordered lists with nesting, and tables.

When comments are included (the default), each comment's anchor text — the specific
text the comment was attached to — is preserved, giving full context for the discussion.

user_google_email.description: User's Google email address

document_id.description:
ID of the Google Doc (or full URL). When a full URL is provided
and it contains a ?tab= query parameter, that tab is used automatically
unless tab_id is also specified (explicit tab_id takes precedence).

comment_mode.description:
How to display comments:
- "inline": Footnote-style references placed at the anchor text location (default)
- "appendix": All comments grouped at the bottom with blockquoted anchor text
- "none": No comments included

include_resolved.description: Whether to include resolved comments (default: False)

suggestions_view_mode.description:
How to render suggestions in the returned content:
- "DEFAULT_FOR_CURRENT_ACCESS": Default based on user's access level
- "SUGGESTIONS_INLINE": Suggested changes appear inline in the document
- "PREVIEW_SUGGESTIONS_ACCEPTED": Preview as if all suggestions were accepted
- "PREVIEW_WITHOUT_SUGGESTIONS": Preview as if all suggestions were rejected

tab_id.description:
Optional ID of a single tab to read (from inspect_doc_structure).
When given, only that tab's content is rendered, without its child tabs
and without a tab heading, and comments are listed as document-wide.
When omitted, every tab is rendered. Pass "" to read every tab of a
URL that carries ?tab=. This filters output only: the whole document
is still fetched.

tools.name: manage_doc_tab
tools.description: Manage document tabs: create, rename, delete, or populate from Markdown.

user_google_email.description: User's Google email address

document_id.description: ID of the document

action.description: Action to perform - "create", "rename", "delete", or "populate_from_markdown"

tab_id.description: Tab ID (required for rename, delete, populate_from_markdown; use inspect_doc_structure to find IDs)

title.description: Tab title (required for create; used by rename)

index.description: Position index for new tab, 0-based among siblings (required for create)

parent_tab_id.description: Optional parent tab ID to nest under (create only)

replace_existing.description: Clear tab body before inserting markdown (default True)

tools.name: list_document_comments
tools.description: List all comments from a Google Document (optional max_comments to limit results).

tools.name: manage_document_comment
tools.description: Manage comments on a Google Document.

tools.name: list_spreadsheets
tools.description: Lists spreadsheets from Google Drive that the user has access to.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

max_results.description: Maximum number of spreadsheets to return. Defaults to 25.

page_token.description: Page token from a previous response's nextPageToken to retrieve the next page of results.

corpora.description:
Corpus to search ('user', 'domain', 'drive', 'allDrives').
Defaults to 'drive' when drive_id is set, otherwise 'allDrives'.

tools.name: get_spreadsheet_info
tools.description: Gets information about a specific spreadsheet including its sheets.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet to get info for. Required.

tools.name: read_sheet_values
tools.description: Reads values from a specific range in a Google Sheet.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

range_name.description:
The range to read (e.g., "Sheet1!A1:D10", "A1:D10").
Defaults to "A1:Z1000". Open-ended or oversized ranges are clamped to
at most 1000 rows before the Sheets API request to bound memory use.

include_hyperlinks.description:
If True, also fetch hyperlink metadata for the range.
Defaults to False to avoid expensive includeGridData requests.

include_notes.description:
If True, also fetch cell notes for the range.
Defaults to False to avoid expensive includeGridData requests.

include_formulas.description:
If True, also fetch raw formula strings for cells that
contain formulas. Useful for identifying cross-sheet references before writing
back to a range. Defaults to False to avoid an extra API request.

include_smart_chips.description:
If True, also fetch smart chips metadata (Drive files/folders
and People chips) for the range. Defaults to False to avoid expensive includeGridData requests.

tools.name: modify_sheet_values
tools.description:
Modifies values in a specific range of a Google Sheet - can write, update, or clear values,
or insert Smart Chips (Drive files/folders or People).

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

values.description: 2D array of values to write/update. Can be a JSON string or Python list. Required unless clear_values=True or chips is provided.

value_input_option.description: How to interpret input values ("RAW" or "USER_ENTERED"). Defaults to "USER_ENTERED".

clear_values.description: If True, clears the range instead of writing values. Defaults to False.

chips.description:
Smart chip(s) to insert instead of values:
- A single URL or email string for a single cell (e.g., "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/123", "user@example.com").
- A list of URLs or emails for a single cell (multiple chips) or across cells (e.g., ["https://...", "https://..."]).
- A 2D list of URLs/emails matching a grid range. For a single-row or single-column
  range, each inner list is instead the chips for one cell (e.g., [["a@x.com", "b@x.com"]]
  puts both chips in the first cell of "A1:C1").
- A dict or list of dicts with explicit properties (e.g., {"type": "drive", "uri": "..."}, {"type": "person", "email": "..."}).
- A JSON-encoded string representing any of the above formats.

chip_type.description: Explicit chip type if passing raw strings in chips: "drive" (default for URLs/IDs) or "person" (default for emails).

tools.name: format_sheet_range
tools.description:
Applies formatting to a range: colors, number formats, text wrapping,
alignment, and text styling.

Colors accept hex strings (#RRGGBB). Number formats follow Sheets types
(e.g., NUMBER, CURRENCY, DATE, PERCENT). If no sheet name is provided,
the first sheet is used.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

range_name.description: A1-style range (optionally with sheet name). Required.

number_format_pattern.description: Custom pattern for the number format.

wrap_strategy.description:
Text wrap strategy - WRAP (wrap text within
cell), CLIP (clip text at cell boundary), or OVERFLOW_CELL (allow text
to overflow into adjacent empty cells).

horizontal_alignment.description:
Horizontal text alignment - LEFT,
CENTER, or RIGHT.

vertical_alignment.description:
Vertical text alignment - TOP, MIDDLE,
or BOTTOM.

tools.name: manage_conditional_formatting
tools.description:
Manages conditional formatting rules on a Google Sheet. Supports adding,
updating, and deleting conditional formatting rules via a single tool.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

action.description:
The operation to perform. Must be one of "add", "update",
or "delete".

range_name.description:
A1-style range (optionally with sheet name).
Required for "add". Optional for "update" (preserves existing ranges
if omitted). Not used for "delete".

condition_type.description:
Sheets condition type (e.g., NUMBER_GREATER,
TEXT_CONTAINS, DATE_BEFORE, CUSTOM_FORMULA). Required for "add".
Optional for "update" (preserves existing type if omitted).

condition_values.description:
Values
for the condition; accepts a list or a JSON string representing a list.
Depends on condition_type. Used by "add" and "update".

background_color.description:
Hex background color to apply when
condition matches. Used by "add" and "update".

text_color.description:
Hex text color to apply when condition matches.
Used by "add" and "update".

rule_index.description:
0-based index of the rule. For "add", optionally
specifies insertion position. Required for "update" and "delete".

gradient_points.description:
List (or JSON list) of
gradient points for a color scale. If provided, a gradient rule is created
and boolean parameters are ignored. Used by "add" and "update".

sheet_name.description:
Sheet name to locate the rule when range_name is
omitted. Defaults to the first sheet. Used by "update" and "delete".

tools.name: create_spreadsheet
tools.description: Creates a new Google Spreadsheet.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

title.description: The title of the new spreadsheet. Required.

sheet_names.description: List of sheet names to create. If not provided, creates one sheet with default name.

folder_id.description:
The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'. For shared
drives, this must be a folder ID within the shared drive.

tools.name: create_sheet
tools.description: Creates a new sheet or duplicates an existing sheet (user_google_email: str, spreadsheet_id: str, sheet_name: Optional[str] = None, source_sheet_name: Optional[str] = None, insert_sheet_index: Optional[int] = None).

tools.name: list_sheet_tables
tools.description:
Lists all structured tables in a spreadsheet with their IDs, names, ranges,
and column details. Use this to find table IDs for append_table_rows.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

tools.name: append_table_rows
tools.description:
Appends rows to a structured table in a Google Sheet. The rows are added
to the end of the table body, automatically extending the table range.

Use list_sheet_tables first to find the table ID.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

table_id.description: The ID of the table to append to (get from list_sheet_tables). Required.

values.description:
2D array of values to append. Each inner
list is one row. Can be a JSON string or Python list. Required.

tools.name: manage_sheet_tab
tools.description:
Manages the lifecycle of an existing sheet tab: rename, delete, hide, unhide or reorder.

Use create_sheet to add a tab, and resize_sheet_dimensions for row and column
level changes. This tool operates on the tab itself.

user_google_email.description: User's Google email address

spreadsheet_id.description: ID of the spreadsheet

sheet_name.description: Title of the existing tab to act on

action.description: One of "rename", "delete", "hide", "unhide", "reorder"

new_index.description: New zero-based position, required for action="reorder"

tools.name: resize_sheet_dimensions
tools.description:
Manages sheet-level dimension properties: resize columns/rows, auto-resize
to fit content, freeze rows/columns, hide/unhide rows/columns, and
insert/delete rows/columns.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

sheet_name.description:
Sheet name to target. Defaults to the
first sheet if not provided.

column_sizes.description:
Dict mapping column letters
to pixel widths. Example: {"A": 200, "C": 300}. Can be a JSON
string or Python dict.

row_sizes.description:
Dict mapping 1-based row
numbers to pixel heights. Example: {"1": 40, "3": 60}. Can be
a JSON string or Python dict.

auto_resize_columns.description:
List of column
letters to auto-resize to fit content. Example: ["A", "B"].

auto_resize_rows.description:
List of 1-based
row numbers to auto-resize to fit content. Example: [1, 2].

frozen_row_count.description:
Number of rows to freeze from the
top. Use 0 to unfreeze all rows.

frozen_column_count.description:
Number of columns to freeze from
the left. Use 0 to unfreeze all columns.

hide_columns.description:
List of column letters
to hide. Example: ["C", "D"].

unhide_columns.description:
List of column
letters to unhide. Example: ["C", "D"].

hide_rows.description:
List of 1-based row
numbers to hide. Example: [3, 4].

unhide_rows.description:
List of 1-based row
numbers to unhide. Example: [3, 4].

insert_rows_at.description:
1-based row number to insert before.
Appends to the end of the sheet if omitted.

insert_columns_at.description:
Column letter to insert before
(e.g. "C"). Appends to the end if omitted.

delete_rows.description:
List of 1-based row
numbers to delete. Example: [5, 6]. Best for non-contiguous rows.

delete_row_range.description:
Contiguous range of rows to delete,
as "start:end" (1-based, inclusive). Example: "5:10" deletes rows
5 through 10. More efficient than delete_rows for large contiguous
ranges.

delete_columns.description:
List of column
letters to delete. Example: ["E", "F"].

tools.name: move_sheet_rows
tools.description:
Moves rows from one sheet to another within the same spreadsheet. The move
is performed in a single batchUpdate (copyPaste followed by
deleteDimension). Note: batchUpdate executes requests sequentially but does
not roll back on partial failure — if the copy succeeds but the delete
fails, rows may be duplicated. Formulas, data types, and formatting are
preserved (unlike a values.get/append round-trip).
Row numbers are 1-based (matching the spreadsheet UI).

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

source_sheet.description: Name of the sheet to move rows from. Required.

start_row.description: First row to move (1-based, inclusive). Required.

end_row.description: Last row to move (1-based, inclusive). Required.

destination_sheet.description: Name of the sheet to move rows to. Required.

tools.name: manage_named_range
tools.description: Manages the lifecycle of named ranges in a Google Sheet: list, create, update, or delete.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

action.description: The operation to perform: "list", "create", "update", or "delete". Required.

name.description: Name for the named range (required for "create"; optional identifier for "update"/"delete").

range_name.description: Target cell or range in A1 notation (e.g., "Sheet1!A1:D10", "A1:B5") (required for "create").

named_range_id.description: The ID of the named range (optional identifier for "update"/"delete").

new_name.description: New name for the named range (used with action="update").

new_range.description: New A1-style range for the named range (used with action="update").

tools.name: list_spreadsheet_comments
tools.description: List all comments from a Google Spreadsheet (optional max_comments to limit results).

tools.name: manage_spreadsheet_comment
tools.description: Manage comments on a Google Spreadsheet.

tools.name: list_spaces
tools.description: Lists Google Chat spaces (rooms and direct messages) accessible to the user.

tools.name: get_messages
tools.description: Retrieves messages from a Google Chat space.

message_filter.description:
Optional filter string using the Chat API filter syntax.
            Supports createTime and thread.name.
            Examples:
              'createTime > "2026-03-18T00:00:00-03:00"'
              'createTime > "2026-03-18T00:00:00-03:00" AND createTime < "2026-03-19T00:00:00-03:00"'
              'thread.name = spaces/X/threads/Y'

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Sends a message to a Google Chat space, or edits a message already sent there.

thread_key.description: Reply in a thread by app-defined key (creates thread if not found).

thread_name.description: Reply in an existing thread by its resource name (e.g. spaces/X/threads/Y).

message_name.description:
Edit this message in place instead of sending a new one
(e.g. spaces/X/messages/Y, as returned by send_message or get_messages).
Must be a message of space_id. Only the text is replaced, and only the
author can edit their own message.

tools.name: search_messages
tools.description: Searches for messages in Google Chat spaces by text content and/or time range.

query.description: Optional text to search for. If omitted, only time_filter is applied.

space_id.description: Optional space to restrict the search to.

page_size.description: Maximum number of messages to return per space.

time_filter.description:
Optional filter using Chat API createTime syntax.
         Examples:
           'createTime > "2026-03-18T00:00:00-03:00"'
           'createTime > "2026-03-18T00:00:00-03:00" AND createTime < "2026-03-19T00:00:00-03:00"'

max_spaces.description: Maximum number of spaces to search when space_id is not provided (default 10).

tools.name: create_reaction
tools.description: Adds an emoji reaction to a Google Chat message.

emoji_unicode.description: The emoji character to react with (e.g. 👍).

tools.name: download_chat_attachment
tools.description:
Downloads an attachment from a Google Chat message and saves it to local disk.

In stdio mode, returns the local file path for direct access.
In HTTP mode, returns a temporary download URL (valid for 1 hour).

attachment_index.description: Zero-based index of the attachment to download (default 0).

tools.name: create_form
tools.description: Create a new form using the title given in the provided form message in the request.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

document_title.description: The document title (shown in browser tab).

tools.name: get_form
tools.description: Get a form.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

form_id.description: The ID of the form to retrieve.

tools.name: set_publish_settings
tools.description: Updates the publish settings of a form.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

form_id.description: The ID of the form to update publish settings for.

is_published.description: Whether the form is published and visible to responders. Defaults to True.

is_accepting_responses.description: Whether the form accepts responses. Only takes effect when the form is published. Defaults to True.

tools.name: get_form_response
tools.description: Get one response from the form.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

response_id.description: The ID of the response to retrieve.

tools.name: list_form_responses
tools.description: List a form's responses.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

page_size.description: Maximum number of responses to return. Defaults to 10.

page_token.description: Token for retrieving next page of results.

tools.name: batch_update_form
tools.description:
Apply batch updates to a Google Form.

Supports adding, updating, and deleting form items, as well as updating
form metadata and settings. This is the primary method for modifying form
content after creation.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

form_id.description: The ID of the form to update.

requests.description:
List of update requests to apply.
Supported request types:
- createItem: Add a new question or content item
- updateItem: Modify an existing item
- deleteItem: Remove an item
- moveItem: Reorder an item
- updateFormInfo: Update form title/description
- updateSettings: Modify form settings (e.g., quiz mode)

tools.name: create_presentation
tools.description: Create a new Google Slides presentation.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

title.description: The title for the new presentation. Defaults to "Untitled Presentation".

tools.name: get_presentation
tools.description: Get details about a Google Slides presentation.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

presentation_id.description: The ID of the presentation to retrieve.

include_speaker_notes.description:
Also report each slide's speaker (presenter)
notes and the object ID of the shape holding them. Pass True when you
need to read or edit notes: that shape ID is the only valid target for
insertText/deleteText on notes, and batch_update_presentation writes
notes by deleting the shape's existing text and inserting new text.
Defaults to False.

include_geometry.description:
Also list each slide's elements with their
placement - transform (translate, and scale/shear when not identity)
and intrinsic size, in raw EMU. Set this when adding slides to an
existing deck so new elements can match its established margins and
content width. Defaults to False.

include_styles.description:
Also list each slide's elements with text styling
(see get_page). Defaults to False.

raw.description:
Return the complete Slides API Presentation resource as JSON
(slides, layouts, masters, notes, every element and style) instead
of the summary. Nothing is filtered, so it can be large; prefer
get_page with raw=True for a single slide. Overrides the other flags.

tools.name: batch_update_presentation
tools.description: Apply batch updates to a Google Slides presentation.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

presentation_id.description: The ID of the presentation to update.

requests.description: List of update requests to apply.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Get details about a specific page (slide) in a presentation.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

page_object_id.description: The object ID of the page/slide to retrieve.

include_geometry.description:
Also report each element's placement - its
transform (translate, and scale/shear when not identity) and intrinsic
size, in raw EMU. Set this when adding elements to an existing deck:
it is the only way to discover the deck's margins, gutters and content
width, which Slides exposes nowhere else, and it reports the same terms
batch_update_presentation writes. Defaults to False to keep the
default output's token cost unchanged. Tables also report column
widths, row heights and cell text.

include_styles.description:
Also report text styling: per paragraph
(alignment, indents, spacing, bullets) and per run of uniform style
(font family, weight, size, bold/italic, color), each with a short
excerpt; plus placeholder linkage, autofit, fill and outline for
shapes (fill=none / outline=none when explicitly not rendered),
and the text styling of every table cell. Only explicitly set
values appear; anything else is inherited from the placeholder
named in the output. Use for proofing: font consistency, color
use, alignment.

raw.description:
Return the complete Slides API Page resource as JSON instead
of the summary. Nothing is filtered. Use when the summary does not
carry a field you need. Overrides the other flags.

tools.name: get_page_thumbnail
tools.description: Generate a thumbnail URL for a specific page (slide) in a presentation.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

page_object_id.description: The object ID of the page/slide.

inline.description:
Also return the rendered PNG itself as image content, so
a multimodal client can look at the slide without fetching the URL.
The URL is a short-lived googleusercontent link that sandboxed or
egress-restricted clients often cannot reach. If the image cannot
be fetched, the URL-only result is returned with a note saying so.
Defaults to False.

tools.name: list_presentation_comments
tools.description: List all comments from a Google Presentation (optional max_comments to limit results).

tools.name: manage_presentation_comment
tools.description: Manage comments on a Google Presentation.

tools.name: list_task_lists
tools.description: List all task lists for the user.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

max_results.description: Maximum number of task lists to return (default: 1000, max: 1000).

page_token.description: Token for pagination.

tools.name: get_task_list
tools.description: Get details of a specific task list.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

task_list_id.description: The ID of the task list to retrieve.

tools.name: manage_task_list
tools.description: Manage task lists: create, update, delete, or clear completed tasks.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

action.description: The action to perform. Must be one of: "create", "update", "delete", "clear_completed".

task_list_id.description: The ID of the task list. Required for "update", "delete", and "clear_completed" actions.

title.description: The title for the task list. Required for "create" and "update" actions.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: List all tasks in a specific task list.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

task_list_id.description: The ID of the task list to retrieve tasks from.

max_results.description: Maximum number of tasks to return. (default: 20, max: 10000).

page_token.description: Token for pagination.

show_completed.description: Whether to include completed tasks (default: True). Note that show_hidden must also be true to show tasks completed in first party clients, such as the web UI and Google's mobile apps.

show_deleted.description: Whether to include deleted tasks (default: False).

show_hidden.description: Whether to include hidden tasks (default: False).

show_assigned.description: Whether to include assigned tasks (default: False).

completed_max.description: Upper bound for completion date (RFC 3339 timestamp).

completed_min.description: Lower bound for completion date (RFC 3339 timestamp).

due_max.description: Upper bound for due date (RFC 3339 timestamp).

due_min.description: Lower bound for due date (RFC 3339 timestamp).

updated_min.description: Lower bound for last modification time (RFC 3339 timestamp).

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: Get details of a specific task.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

task_list_id.description: The ID of the task list containing the task.

task_id.description: The ID of the task to retrieve.

tools.name: manage_task
tools.description: Manage tasks: create, update, delete, or move tasks within task lists.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

action.description: The action to perform. Must be one of: "create", "update", "delete", "move".

task_list_id.description: The ID of the task list. Required for all actions.

task_id.description: The ID of the task. Required for "update", "delete", and "move" actions.

title.description: The title of the task. Required for "create", optional for "update".

notes.description: Notes/description for the task. Used by "create" and "update" actions.

status.description: Task status ("needsAction" or "completed"). Used by "update" action.

due.description: Due date in RFC 3339 format (e.g., "2024-12-31T23:59:59Z"). Used by "create" and "update" actions.

parent.description: Parent task ID (for subtasks). Used by "create" and "move" actions.

previous.description: Previous sibling task ID (for positioning). Used by "create" and "move" actions.

destination_task_list.description: Destination task list ID (for moving between lists). Used by "move" action.

tools.name: list_contacts
tools.description: List contacts for the authenticated user.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

page_size.description: Maximum number of contacts to return (default: 100, max: 1000).

page_token.description: Token for pagination.

tools.name: get_contact
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific contact.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

contact_id.description: The contact ID (e.g., "c1234567890" or full resource name "people/c1234567890").

tools.name: search_contacts
tools.description: Search contacts by name, email, phone number, or other fields.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

query.description: Search query string (searches names, emails, phone numbers).

page_size.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 30, max: 30).

tools.name: manage_contact
tools.description:
Create, update, or delete a contact. Consolidated tool replacing create_contact,

tools.name: generate_trigger_code
tools.description:
Generates Apps Script code for creating triggers.

The Apps Script API cannot create triggers directly - they must be created
from within Apps Script itself. This tool generates the code you need.
To list or remove existing triggers without opening the editor, use
`manage_script_trigger` (action="list" / action="delete") instead.

trigger_type.description:
Type of trigger. One of:
          - "time_minutes" (run every N minutes: 1, 5, 10, 15, 30)
          - "time_hours" (run every N hours: 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12)
          - "time_daily" (run daily at a specific hour: 0-23)
          - "time_weekly" (run weekly on a specific day)
          - "on_open" (simple trigger - runs when document opens)
          - "on_edit" (simple trigger - runs when user edits)
          - "on_form_submit" (runs when form is submitted)
          - "on_change" (runs when content changes)

function_name.description: The function to run when trigger fires (e.g., "sendDailyReport")

schedule.description:
Schedule details (depends on trigger_type):
      - For time_minutes: "1", "5", "10", "15", or "30"
      - For time_hours: "1", "2", "4", "6", "8", or "12"
      - For time_daily: hour as "0"-"23" (e.g., "9" for 9am)
      - For time_weekly: "MONDAY", "TUESDAY", etc.
      - For simple triggers (on_open, on_edit): not needed

tools.name: manage_script_trigger
tools.description:
List or delete the current user's installable triggers on a script project.

The Apps Script REST API has no triggers resource, so in dev_mode both actions
provision (or refresh) a small helper file and run it via the Execution
API - the only way to inspect or change trigger state without opening the
editor. Neither action is read-only: the helper file may be written into the
project on first use. To create a trigger, use `generate_trigger_code` to
produce the setup code, add it with `manage_script_content`, then run it with
`run_script_function`.

Delete all triggers calling this function name
(delete only).

dev_mode.description:
Run against the latest saved code (default; project owner
only) vs. the deployed version. False requires the helper to
already exist in the deployed version.

deployment_id.description:
Optional API Executable deployment ID. When omitted, the
highest versioned API Executable deployment is used.

assignees.description: Usernames to assign to this issue

body.description: Issue body content

duplicate_of.description: Issue number that this issue is a duplicate of. Required when state_reason is 'duplicate'.

delete.description: Set to true to clear this field's current value on the issue. When false or omitted, this property is ignored. Cannot be true when 'value' or 'field_option_name' is provided.

field_name.description: Issue field name (case-insensitive). Must match a field returned by list_issue_fields for this repository or its organization.

field_option_name.description: Option name for single-select fields. Validated against the field's options before the API call. Cannot be combined with 'value' or 'delete: true'.

value.description: Value to set. Use for text, number, and date fields (date as YYYY-MM-DD). For single-select fields, prefer 'field_option_name' so the option is validated before the API call. Cannot be combined with 'field_option_name' or 'delete: true'.

issue_fields.description: Issue field values to set or clear. Each item requires 'field_name' and exactly one of 'value', 'field_option_name', or 'delete: true'.

labels.description: Labels to apply to this issue

method.description:
Write operation to perform on a single issue.
Options are:
- 'create' - creates a new issue.
- 'update' - updates an existing issue.

parent_issue_number.description: Issue number of the parent issue. Only used when method is 'create' and cannot be combined with issue_fields. The new issue is created and attached to this parent in the same operation.

parent_owner.description: Repository owner of the parent issue. Must be provided with parent_repo. Omit both to use owner and repo. Only used when method is 'create' and parent_issue_number is provided.

parent_repo.description: Repository name of the parent issue. Must be provided with parent_owner. Omit both to use owner and repo. Only used when method is 'create' and parent_issue_number is provided.

state_reason.description: Reason for the state change. Ignored unless state is changed.

type.description: Type of this issue. For updates, pass null to remove the current type. Only use if issue types are enabled for this repository. Use list_issue_types to get valid type values for this repository or its owner organization. If the repository doesn't support issue types, omit this parameter.

tools.description: Get information on a specific pull request in GitHub repository.

after.description: Cursor for pagination, used only by the get_review_comments method. Pass the endCursor from the previous page's PageInfo to fetch the next page.

method.description:
Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. 
Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 9. get_check_runs - Get check runs for the head commit of a pull request. Check runs are the individual CI/CD jobs and checks that run on the PR.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

body.description: Review comment text

method.description: The write operation to perform on pull request review.

threadId.description: The node ID of the review thread (e.g., PRRT_kwDOxxx). Required for resolve_thread and unresolve_thread methods. Get thread IDs from pull_request_read with method get_review_comments.

tools.description: Fast and precise code search across ALL GitHub repositories using GitHub's native search engine. Best for finding exact symbols, functions, classes, or specific code patterns.

fields.description: Subset of fields to return for each code search result. If omitted, all fields are returned. Use this to reduce response size when you only need specific fields; omitting 'repository' and 'text_matches' in particular drops the largest per-result data.

query.description: Search query (GitHub code search REST). Implicit AND between terms; supports `OR`, `NOT`, and `"quoted phrase"` for exact match. Qualifiers: `repo:owner/repo`, `org:`, `user:`, `language:`, `path:dir` (prefix match), `filename:exact.ext`, `extension:`, `in:file`, `in:path`, `size:`, `is:archived`, `is:fork`. Max 256 chars. Examples: `WithContext language:go org:github`; `"package main" repo:o/r`; `func extension:go path:cmd repo:o/r`; `NOT TODO language:go repo:o/r`.

query.description: Commit search query (GitHub commit search REST). Searches commit messages on the default branch only. Scope the search with `repo:owner/repo`, `org:`, or `user:` (queries without a scope qualifier match across all of GitHub and are usually not what you want). Other qualifiers: `author:`, `committer:`, `author-name:`, `committer-name:`, `author-email:`, `committer-email:`, `author-date:`, `committer-date:` (supports `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, and `YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD` ranges), `merge:true|false`, `hash:`, `tree:`, `parent:`, `is:public`. Examples: `repo:owner/repo fix panic`; `org:github author:defunkt committer-date:>=2024-01-01`; `"refactor cache" repo:o/r`; `hash:abc1234 repo:o/r`.

sort.description: Sort by author or committer date (defaults to best match)

tools.description: Add a sub-issue to a parent issue in a GitHub repository.

after_id.description: The ID of the sub-issue to be prioritized after (either after_id OR before_id should be specified)

method.description:
The action to perform on a single sub-issue
Options are:
- 'add' - add a sub-issue to a parent issue in a GitHub repository.
- 'remove' - remove a sub-issue from a parent issue in a GitHub repository.
- 'reprioritize' - change the order of sub-issues within a parent issue in a GitHub repository. Use either 'after_id' or 'before_id' to specify the new position.
Writes issue hierarchy. To move a sub-issue to a new parent, use `add` with `replace_parent=true`; there is no writable parent field.

replace_parent.description: When true, replaces the sub-issue's current parent issue. Use with 'add' method only.

method.description:
Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. 
Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 9. get_check_runs - Get check runs for the head commit of a pull request. Check runs are the individual CI/CD jobs and checks that run on the PR.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

body.description: Review comment text

method.description: The write operation to perform on pull request review.

channels.description: New default channel IDs (comma-separated). Replaces existing default channels.

handle.description: New @mention handle (without @). Changing this changes how users mention the group.

name.description: New display name for the group.

usergroup_id.description: ID of the user group to update (starts with 'S', e.g., 'S0123456789'). Get IDs from usergroups_list.

usergroup_id.description: ID of the user group (starts with 'S', e.g., 'S0123456789'). Get IDs from usergroups_list.

tools.name: add_activity_to_incident
tools.description: Add a note (userNote activity) to an existing incident's timeline using its ID. The note body can include URLs which will be attached as context. Use this to add context to an incident.

tools.name: alerting_manage_routing
tools.description:
Manage Grafana alerting routing configuration, including notification policies, contact points and time intervals.

Notification policies define how alerts are grouped, routed, and which contact points receive them.
Time intervals define active/mute periods for alert notifications.

When to use:
- Understanding how alerts are routed to contact points/receivers
- Debugging why an alert went to a specific receiver
- Checking grouping, timing, or mute interval settings

When NOT to use:
- Checking alert rule configuration or state (use alerting_manage_rules)

contact_point_title.description: Title of the contact point to retrieve (required for get_contact_point operation)

datasource_uid.description: Optional: UID of an Alertmanager-compatible datasource to query for receivers. If omitted, returns Grafana-managed contact points. Only used with get_contact_points.

limit.description: The maximum number of results to return. Default is 100. Only used with get_contact_points.

name.description: Filter contact points by name (exact match). Only used with get_contact_points.

operation.description: The operation to perform: 'get_notification_policies' to retrieve the notification policy tree, 'get_contact_points' to list all contact points, 'get_contact_point' to get a specific contact point by name, 'get_time_intervals' to list all time intervals, 'get_time_interval' to get a specific time interval by name

time_interval_name.description: Name of the time interval to retrieve (required for get_time_interval operation)

tools.name: alerting_manage_rules
tools.description:
Manage Grafana alert rules with full CRUD capabilities and filtering.

When to use:
- Understanding why an alert is or isn't firing
- Auditing alert rule configuration (queries, conditions, labels, notification settings)
- Finding alert rules by state, folder, group, or name
- Creating, updating, or deleting alert rules
- Comparing rule versions to see what changed

When NOT to use:
- Checking how alerts are routed to receivers (use alerting_manage_routing)

annotations.description: Optional annotations for the alert rule

condition.description: The query condition identifier, e.g. 'A', 'B' (required for 'create', 'update')

data.description: Array of alert query objects (required for 'create'/'update'). Each object has: datasourceUid (string, required), model (object with expr for data queries or type/expression/conditions for expressions), refId (string, auto-assigned if omitted), relativeTimeRange ({from, to} in seconds, defaults to {from:600,to:0}). For server-side expressions use datasourceUid '__expr__'. Example: [{datasourceUid: 'prometheus', model: {expr: 'up == 0'}}, {datasourceUid: '__expr__', model: {type: 'threshold', expression: 'A', conditions: [{evaluator: {type: 'gt', params: [0]}}]}}]

datasource_uid.description: Optional: UID of a Prometheus or Loki datasource to query for datasource-managed alert rules (for 'list' operation)

disable_provenance.description: If true, the alert remains editable in the Grafana UI (sets X-Disable-Provenance header). Defaults to true.

exec_err_state.description: State on execution error: NoData, Alerting, OK (required for 'create', 'update')

folder_uid.description: The folder UID. For 'list': filter by exact folder UID (mutually exclusive with search_folder). For 'create'/'update': the folder to store the rule in (required).

for.description: Duration before alert fires, e.g. '5m' (required for 'create', 'update')

is_paused.description: If true, the alert rule remains inactive, Default is false

keep_firing_for.description: Enables continous firing of alert for specified time even when condition is no longer met. Default is 0 (resolves immediately)

label_selectors.description: Prometheus-style selectors to filter alert rules by labels. Each string is a selector e.g. '{severity="critical", team=~"backend.*"}'. All selectors must match (AND).

labels.description: Optional labels for the alert rule

limit_alerts.description: Limit alert instances per rule. For list: 0 omits alerts. For get: <=0 defaults to 200. Max 200.

matchers.description: Label matchers to filter alert instances. Each string is a Prometheus-style matcher e.g. 'severity="critical"', 'env!="dev"', 'team=~"backend.*"'. Requires Grafana 12.4+.

missing_series_evals_to_resolve.description: Consecutive evaluation intervals with no data required to mark the alert as resolved. Default is 2.

no_data_state.description: State when no data: NoData, Alerting, OK (required for 'create', 'update')

notification_settings.description: Notification settings object. Fields: receiver (string, required), groupBy ([]string), groupWait/groupInterval/repeatInterval (duration strings), muteTimeIntervals/activeTimeIntervals ([]string).

operation.description: The operation to perform: 'list', 'get', 'versions', 'create', 'update', or 'delete'. To create a rule, use operation 'create' and provide all required fields in a single call. To update a rule, first use 'get' to retrieve its full configuration, then 'update' with all required fields plus your changes.

record.description: Recording rule config. Fields: from (string, required - ref ID e.g. 'A'), metric (string, required - metric name), targetDatasourceUid (string, optional).

rule_limit.description: Maximum number of rules to return (default 200, max 200). Requires Grafana 12.4+ (for 'list' operation)

rule_uid.description: The UID of the alert rule (required for 'get', 'versions', 'update', 'delete'; optional for 'create')

search_folder.description: Search folders by path using partial matching (for 'list' operation). Requires Grafana 12.4+. Mutually exclusive with folder_uid.

search_rule_name.description: Search alert rule names/titles using partial matching. Requires Grafana 12.4+ (for 'list' operation)

states.description: Filter by alert state: firing, pending, normal, recovering, nodata, error (for 'list' operation)

title.description: The title of the alert rule (required for 'create', 'update')

comment.description: A human-readable comment explaining the silence (required for 'create' and 'update')

created_by.description: Author of the silence. Defaults to 'grafana-assistant'.

ends_at.description: Silence end time in RFC3339 format, e.g. '2026-07-11T12:00:00Z' (required for 'create' and 'update')

value.description: The label value to match against

isRegex.description: Whether value is a regular expression. Defaults to false.

isEqual.description: Whether the matcher asserts equality (true) or inequality (false). Defaults to true.

matchers.description: Label matchers. Required (at least one) for 'create' and 'update'. For 'list', used as an optional filter.

operation.description: The operation to perform: 'list' to list silences, 'get' to retrieve a silence by id, 'create' to create a new silence, 'update' to modify an existing silence by id, 'delete' to expire a silence by id

rule_uid.description: Optional: filter listed silences to those scoped to this alert rule UID (matches the __alert_rule_uid__ label). Only used with 'list'.

starts_at.description: Silence start time in RFC3339 format, e.g. '2026-07-11T10:00:00Z' (required for 'create' and 'update'). Grafana clamps a start time in the past to the moment of creation, so for 'update' pass back the starts_at returned by 'get' to keep the silence id stable.

tools.name: create_datasource
tools.description: Create a datasource. If type is ambiguous, call search_plugin_information first; install the plugin if needed. IMPORTANT: always call this tool twice. First call: provide only the type вЂ” the tool returns a field schema. After receiving the schema, you MUST ask the user for every required field value explicitly; do not infer or use defaults without user confirmation. Second call: provide the type, the display name in the top-level name argument, schemaReviewed=true, and the fields map populated with values confirmed by the user. Never handle credentials вЂ” remind the user to rotate any detected. Returns UID, health check, and a config page link.

schemaReviewed.description: Set to true on the second call to confirm you reviewed the schema and collected values from the user.

url.description: Datasource base URL when required by the plugin

withCredentials.description: Whether Grafana should forward credentials such as cookies

parentUid.description: Optional parent folder UID. If set, the folder will be created under this parent.

uid.description: Optional folder UID. If omitted, Grafana will generate one.

tools.name: create_incident
tools.description: Create a new Grafana incident. Requires title, severity, and room prefix. Allows setting status, labels and custom fields. This tool should be used judiciously and sparingly, and only after confirmation from the user, as it may notify or alarm lots of people.

tools.name: find_slow_requests

end.description: End time for the investigation. Defaults to now if not specified.

labelSelector.description: A PromQL/LogQL stream selector to scope the analysis. Supports all match operators: = (exact), != (not equal), =~ (regex), !~ (negative regex). Example: {namespace=~"prod.*", cluster="us-east-1"}

start.description: Start time for the investigation. Defaults to 30 minutes ago if not specified.

tools.name: generate_deeplink
tools.description: Generate deeplink URLs for Grafana resources. Supports dashboards (requires dashboardUid or provisioningPreview), panels (requires dashboardUid or provisioningPreview, plus panelId), and Explore queries (requires datasourceUid and optionally queries). For dashboard and panel links, provisioningPreview points at a dashboard staged on a provisioning repository branch (e.g. a git-sync PR preview). For explore links, the time range and queries are embedded inside the Grafana explore state. Set shorten=true to also attempt a /goto/<uid> short URL; if shortening fails, the full deeplink is returned.

queries.description: List of query objects for explore links (e.g. [{"refId":"A","expr":"up"}])

queryParams.description: Additional URL query parameters (for dashboard/panel types)

resourceType.description: Type of resource: dashboard, panel, or explore

shorten.description: If true, try to shorten the generated URL to /goto/<uid>. If shortening fails, return the original deeplink.

tools.name: get_alert_group
tools.description: Get a specific alert group from Grafana OnCall by its ID. Returns the full alert group details, including the most recent alert and its raw payload when the OnCall API provides them. Alert payloads carry integration-specific fingerprints (for example Sentry's payload.data.event.hashes or Alertmanager's payload.alerts[].fingerprint) that identify recurring alerts across different alert groups.

alertGroupId.description: The ID of the alert group to retrieve

tools.name: get_annotation_tags
tools.description: Returns annotation tags with optional filtering by tag name. Only the provided filters are applied.

limit.description: Max results, default 100

tools.name: get_dashboard_by_uid
tools.description: Retrieves the complete dashboard, including panels, variables, and settings, for a specific dashboard identified by its UID. Pass optional version to load a saved snapshot instead of the current dashboard. Saved snapshots are fetched through Grafana's legacy versions API, so 'apiVersion' is omitted and 'meta' is partial: only version, createdBy, and created are populated. For current (non-versioned) fetches, the response includes 'apiVersion' and 'isV2': when 'isV2' is true the dashboard uses the v2 schema (panels live under 'elements' keyed by name, arranged by 'layout'; variables under 'variables'), otherwise it is classic v1 ('panels[]' with 'templating.list'). WARNING: Large dashboards can consume significant context window space. Consider using get_dashboard_summary for overview or get_dashboard_property for specific data instead.

version.description: Optional saved version. Omit for the current dashboard

tools.name: get_dashboard_panel_queries
tools.description: Retrieve panel queries from a Grafana dashboard. Supports all datasource types (Prometheus, Loki, CloudWatch, SQL, etc.) and row-nested panels. Optionally filter to a specific panel by ID with `panelId`. Optionally provide `variables` for template variable substitution, which populates `processedQuery` and `requiredVariables` fields. Returns an array of objects with fields: title, query (raw expression), datasource (object with uid and type), and optionally processedQuery, refId, requiredVariables, and target. Targets built in a visual editor (CloudWatch metric search, InfluxDB query builder) have no string expression: those return an empty query plus `target`, the panel's raw query JSON. Run those with run_panel_query rather than a query tool.

panelId.description: Optional panel ID to filter to a specific panel

tools.name: get_dashboard_property
tools.description: Get specific parts of a dashboard using JSONPath expressions to minimize context window usage. JSONPath targets the dashboard's native schema. Classic v1 paths: '$.title' (title)\, '$.panels[*].title' (all panel titles)\, '$.panels[0]' (first panel)\, '$.templating.list' (variables)\, '$.annotations.list' (saved dashboard annotation queries/definitions)\, '$.tags' (tags)\, '$.panels[*].targets[*].expr' (all queries). v2 dashboards (see isV2 from get_dashboard_by_uid) use different paths: '$.title'\, '$.elements' (panels\, keyed by name)\, '$.variables' (variables)\, '$.annotations'. Use this instead of get_dashboard_by_uid when you only need specific dashboard properties.

jsonPath.description: JSONPath expression to extract specific data (e.g., '$.panels[0].title' for first panel title, '$.panels[*].title' for all panel titles, '$.templating.list' for variables, '$.annotations.list' for saved dashboard annotation queries/definitions)
